This is a continuation from the final episode of *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*. It’s the “True Tutorial” arc.
=====
“Father! Big Sister! Filo-oooooo! Wait for meeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”
I barely managed to catch up to Father’s cart as it raced away. But after glancing at me with a face like he’d just swallowed a bitter pill, he turned his gaze forward with a tense expression.
“Filo! Run faster!”
“G-Guaaaaaaaah!”
Filo-tan showed some real grit at Father’s request! This is it! She’s actually enjoying this game of tag with me! Woaaaaah, I won’t lose!
Just as I was thinking that and showing off my leg strength to Filo-tan and my Father, the cart jolted, and the figure sitting on the back looked like it was about to tumble off. Oh, that’s my sister! Isn’t that a little dangerous?
“Raphtalia! Are you okay!?”
“U… uh…”
She looked completely drained and was about to fall off at any moment. She seems to be in pretty bad shape.
“Here we go!”
I gave her a gentle shove to get her back onto the cart, then hopped on myself.
“I caught up to you! I win this game of tag!”
“Tch… He’s not even out of breath.”
And so, my father pulled on the reins and stopped Filo-chan. Then, while holding his shield in a defensive stance, he kept glancing over at my sister. What kind of reaction is this, I wonder?
“What’s the matter?”
“Send Raphtalia over here.”
“Yes, sir. She doesn’t look well.”
Following Father’s instructions, I handed my sister over to him. Seeing my attitude, my Father furrowed his brow and tilted his head.
“Would you like me to cast an anti-nausea spell or a Recovery spell?”
“Are you planning to make Raphtalia drink poison!?”
Poison? Why on earth would I need to make my Older Sister drink poison? If anyone’s going to drink it, it should be the Crimson Swine. I’d like to make him drink a poison that makes him writhe in agony, just like what he did to Fleon-chan. Well, he’s already out of this world, though. HAHAHA.
“I wouldn’t do such a thing. You don’t look too well, so you should probably get some rest.”
“You’re the one saying that! Who do you think is to blame for us having to run away!?”
Let me think about it. …No matter how I look at it, I can’t think of anyone but Crimson Swine!
“It’s Crimson Swine’s fault! I’ll never forgive that guy!”
“No! It’s your fault for killing him!”
“Hahaha, wasn’t it because you, Father, demanded I take him out?”
“I never said that! I was just thinking it!”
Oh, he’s even more hostile than the Father in my memories. In my hazy memories, my Father used to sigh a lot when talking to me and always seemed gloomy. However, it’s the greatest honor to be able to sense what’s really on his mind. I’ll keep this up and prove myself to be his right-hand man!
“Well, the Lazy Pig got away, but that’s a trivial matter.”
“What do you mean, a trivial matter…? Are you really okay? In every way?”
As he said that, my Father looked at me with concern. This Motoyasu—tears of emotion are welling up in my eyes. Unlike in the previous loop, you still have a kind heart that wants to be closer to the Father from the first world! That’s exactly the kind of Father you are. I’ll follow you wherever you go!
“Oh! That worried look in Father’s eyes! I, Motoyasu, am truly delighted!”
“That’s why I told you to stop fooling around!　Oh, for heaven’s sake!”
“Guh?”
Oh? Filo-chan seems concerned about us and is looking this way, glancing around. Leave it to me, Filo-chan. I’ll definitely show you the path to glory alongside my Father… the Filolial Road.
“Ugh… w-what happened?”
My sister, who had been slumped over, opened her eyes and turned toward Father. Then, realizing I was there, she staggered and tried to stand up hurriedly. Her expression was pained, but it was also clearly on guard. Hmm… Why am I being treated with such suspicion?
“Actually, a little while ago… when Filo kicked Motoyasu—who was laughing his head off—that bastard snapped, started babbling nonsense, and went and killed that woman right in front of me.”
“Huh!? R-really!?”
“Yeah, I’m not exaggerating. He really did kill her with that spear.”
The older sister looked at me with a shocked expression. So, I gave a firm nod. It’s an undeniable fact, after all. The Crimson Swine is a being unworthy of living in this world. In fact, the longer he stays alive, the more vitality is drained from the world.
“I’m not lying, you know? I killed that scourge of the world, the Crimson Swine!”
The surprised Older Sister looked at my Father, and he nodded silently. She’s still staring at me with a look that says she can’t believe it. All right, I should have made it clear by now that I’m on her side. From here on out, I’ll prove that I’m someone she can trust.
“The orders of my Father are absolute. That’s the condition for making you part of our team, after all.”
“Father? Naofumi-sama, did you set a condition for letting him join us?”
“I didn’t say that! He’s been acting like this the whole time. Can’t you do something about it?!”
My father is running his fingers through his hair. You’ll damage your cuticles if you keep doing that!
“W-what on earth… What do you mean, ‘strange’?”
“I’ve come from the future, and I know everything. The shock from earlier brought it all back to me.”
“The future…?”
My Older Sister is looking at me with furrowed brows. Well, I suppose it’s hard to make her believe me right away. But I’ll keep talking patiently, just like in the previous loop. Because I believe that’s the true path to peace.
“So you knew all that and still killed him?”
“He’s a menace—there’s not the slightest reason to let him live.”
“Well, I agree with that… but I’ll be the one taking the blame for killing that woman, won’t I!”
“Is there a problem with taking the blame?”
“Of course there is! You’re planning to frame me again, aren’t you?!”
Oh? Father’s reaction… Ah, come to think of it, he doesn’t know the real reason why he’s been framed. In that case, I suppose I’d best start by explaining that.
“Um, what do you mean by ‘Father’?”
“Because you’re Filo-chan’s Father, of course.”
“Guh?”
“Filo’s… well, considering your relationship with Naofumi-sama, I suppose you could be considered Filo’s foster father…”
It seems my sister is also starting to recover from her motion sickness.
“So, Father, don’t you want to know why you were falsely accused of rape?”
At my question, Father glared at me intensely while clenching his fists. Then, as if choosing his words carefully, he said:
“…What do you know? What are you trying to say with that mocking attitude?”
“It’s the truth I learned from the future. Of course, the things I did without realizing it are facts that can’t be changed, but I’m truly remorseful.”
“Just spit it out. Well… since you wiped that guy out, I suppose I might as well hear you out a little.”
“You believe me!?”
“You can’t just pull off a massacre right in front of me and get away with a ‘Hehehe, just kidding.’ At the very least, the Motoyasu I’ve known up until now would never have done something like that.”
“That’s… true.”
Just as I expected from my Father. You really do know me well. My sister seems convinced, too. It’s true—the me before I recalled my memories of the future would never have killed Crimson Swine. I’ll use this as a breakthrough to gain their trust!
“Whether I end up messing up again or manage to get away with this, since Filo ran after me and caught up, I have no choice but to listen to what he has to say.”
He’s quick to assess the situation. I’d like to learn from that.
“Then I’ll tell you. This country, Melromarc, has a state religion that regards the Shield Hero as the enemy.”

Oh, Filo-chan… the way you tilt your little head like that is absolutely adorable! I’d love to record that voice on a sound-recording crystal and listen to it 24 hours a day, 365 days a year! When do you sleep? HAHAHA, I’d want to listen to it even while you’re sleeping.
Plus, in the future, your schedule was so busy you couldn’t even meet me, but it seems you’re not quite that busy right now. I’d really like to get along well with you, Filo-chan. But before that, I’ll have to get permission from your Father. I’ll have to explain things thoroughly.

My father is keeping a wary eye on me while consulting with my sister. I guess he still doesn’t believe me.
“Well, it wasn’t my head that got hit—it was my groin… So, is that silly saying true—that a womanizer’s brain is in his groin…?”
My father is wearing a rather ambiguous expression. This isn’t looking good. At this rate, he might not trust me. Alright, how about I get my sister to help persuade him too?
“Big Sister”
“Eh… Based on the order in which we’ve been taking care of Naofumi-sama, does that mean I’m ‘Big Sister’ because I’m Filo’s Older Sister?”

As expected of Big Sister, you’re very perceptive. You are, after all, Filo-chan’s Older Sister.

“Now it’s my turn, is it…?”
“What are you planning to say?”

Oh? That backfired, didn’t it? Big Sis’s guard is up now. I feel like my Father from the first world is saying, “You’re still just as stupid as ever.” That’s not true! I’m not stupid! I’m just faithful to love!

“So I just missed the mark and ended up looking like an idiot after all…”
“Please wait! Please hear me out! I made a mistake!”
“We’ll see about that…”
Come on, R'yne! I’m experiencing an endorphin rush! Ha… Knowledge from a loop I experienced before raced through my mind, and a brilliant idea struck me.
“I know the names of the villagers where my older sister used to live, and I know she has an Older Sister!”
“Oh, really… Does Raphtalia have an Older Sister?”
Huh? My father seems interested. She’s here, she’s here. The Older Sister of that super-strong orca therianthrope’s Older Sister.
“An Older Sister?”
“Doesn’t she have one?”
“She must have one! She’s the Older Sister of that orca therianthrope who used Lightning Magic and worked as a fisherman in the neighborhood!”

Guh… I suppose that’s not entirely out of the question. Then my Father started whispering with my older sister. But with these enhanced ears—the Motoyasu Ears—I can pick up even the faintest whispers! Motoyasu Ears! Full Drive!
“What do you think?”
Alright, I can make out every word perfectly. This means I’m not left out of the loop anymore!
“It’s way too outlandish to be a lie… Motoyasu isn’t an idiot… no, normally he’d tell a much better lie, right?”
“Why did you stop halfway through?”
“If that wasn’t an act, then he’s just a complete idiot right now.”
“…You’re right.”
“Or rather, was it the future…? If he really could use such a powerful skill, it does make you wonder why he didn’t use it in the duel…”
Of course, there’s no way I could have used Brionac at that point. I knew from the game’s lore that I’d eventually be able to use it, though. It’s a shameful past—I foolishly turned my blade against my Father, who had such low attack power, and ended up losing. On top of that, the Crimson Swine used underhanded tactics to tarnish the sacred duel. He’s gone now, but he was a filthy scum of a man—no matter how many times I killed him, it still wouldn’t have been enough.
Anyway, I turned over a new leaf and swore to fight for the peaceful world that Father and Filo are striving for. This oath is an eternal pact that will never falter—not even after the world achieves peace… or even if a new loop begins!
“W-well, if you have some sort of plan, that’s fine…”
“But you’re not planning to kill that woman or make Filo your bride, are you? You don’t seem to have any intention of convincing us.”
“It’s strange in so many ways, isn’t it? As for whether that story about you coming from the future is actually true… why don’t you test it out a little more?”
“Hmm… Well… I do have a slight hunch. What should I do…? It’s a revelation that the unreasonable things happening to me are actually caused by religion, but…”
You seem troubled. I suppose there’s nothing to be done about it.
“Then, as proof that I’m joining you, I’ll hand over my entire fortune.”
I reached into my pocket and handed my Father a money pouch. I don’t know how much is in it, but it’s just pocket change anyway. Since I’m going to be handing over all my money to my Father anyway, if this helps me gain even a little trust, it’s a win. My Father took my money and his eyes widened even more.
“You’re just going to say it got stolen, aren’t you!”
“I won’t say that. If I did, Father and Filo would end up hating me. If you want, I’ll earn more and bring it back.”
If I can build trust with money, so be it. Here we go—the tribute! Tribute, tribute—a mountain of gold coins!
“……”
At my words, my Father fell silent and began checking the contents of the money bag. Given that it’s been a few days since the first wave ended, there should be a decent amount in there. Well, I figure I could easily earn this much by wiping out griffins in the mountains or hunting down bandits. I’ll work like a workhorse to contribute to you, Father! The fact that the “workhorse” analogy shares a common spirit with Lady Filolial is quite appealing.
“So, Father. What should we do next?”

Kou transformed into an angel right then and there and called out to the squirrel-like Beastman child.

“The shopping district.”

The squirrel-like Beastman child nodded in agreement at Kou’s suggestion.

“Whoa! That’s amazing! You’re so strong!”
“Yep. Kou’s strong! So, do you think we’ll find your mom?”
“Huh? Hmm… I can’t see her.”
“Then let’s go this way. Kitamura, come on!”
“Got it! Where could this kid’s mom be? She’s lost!”
And so, we made our way through the shopping district, searching for the lost child’s parent. However, far from finding the child’s parent, we end up getting swept up in the lively crowd.
“Hmm… Hey, this might surprise you a bit, but please don’t struggle—it’s dangerous.”
“Huh? Okay.”
Kou gently explains the situation to the lost child, and after getting their consent, he transforms into the Filolial King. With a “puff,” he changes form, startling those around him. Though in Siltvelt, where there are many Beastmen and others who can transform, people don’t seem all that surprised. Still, combined with his striking height, Kou now stands out even in the crowd.
“Is anyone here this child’s mom?”
“Here, right here!”
I can see a hand raised somewhere in the crowd.
“Ah! It’s her mom!”
And just like that, the lost child’s parent was found in a flash.

The Beastman, the child’s parent, bows to me—Kou’s guardian. Since everyone in the kingdom knows I’m the Spear Hero, she was so surprised she nearly fell over.
“I’m glad nothing serious happened.”
“That’s a relief.”
“Thanks a lot!”
“W-well then… I’ll repay you someday.”
“Don’t worry about it.”
“Well then.”
And so, we waved goodbye to the squirrel Beastman and his child and left the scene.

Kou walks along the path back to the castle, humming to himself. But… seeing that exchange just now, I’m really happy that Kou has grown into such a kind-hearted child.
Suddenly, the image of Kou—who had been fiercely scolded by my Father after suggesting he wanted to eat a Mole—flashed through my mind.
That’s right. There’s a terrifying incident here that haunts Kou’s psyche. Without his Big Sister or her friends around, Kou would probably start saying he wants to eat little Beastmen.

Melon seems troubled. I’m not trying to trouble Melon… I mean, the elephant. I just want to repay the favor he did me by guiding Kou.

For some reason, Panda said this with a distant look in his eyes. What’s that about!? Does he have a complaint against Filolial-sama or something?

Even Éclair agrees. My Father is giving a wry smile.

“No, I didn’t.”

Kou looks a little embarrassed after being praised by me and my Father.

I did wonder why a Rival had to come up at that moment, but since she’s stuck in the same loop as me, she probably just wants to hear a different perspective.

I suppose that’s just because Kou’s a boy. It feels like he’s arguing back because someone pointed out a weakness he hasn’t experienced yet.

You mustn’t traumatize Kou by saying the wrong thing! But thanks to Zou, we can rest easy now.

…It feels like we’ve turned into little people inside this mansion. Everything is huge. Everything in this room is extra-large. There’s a desk, and there’s a bookshelf, too.

Father points at the door and smiles. Then he walks over to the window and looks outside. The view is nice. There are large fields and such—the land seems fertile. It’s a bit on the chilly side, though. Looking toward the mountains, it looks like there’s still some snow left.

Hmm, that’s true—at that rate, he probably won’t slip up in front of my Father. In terms of gathering information, Zou might be right. Zou places his hand on the doorknob with a slightly anxious gait.
“Elmero, are you okay?”
Kou asks with concern. Zou turns around and gives a faint smile.
“Yes, I’m fine.”
With a click, Zou left the room.
“I’m kind of worried…”

“Indeed. If he’d lived here before, I’m sure he’d know it by heart.”
Yuki-chan replies while checking the mansion’s decorations. It’s true—I can’t imagine someone rebuilding such a large mansion over and over again. Not knowing the layout of that mansion is proof that he’s only lived there for a short enough time to not know it.

I feel like I’ve caught a glimpse of the Darkness surrounding the elephant’s house.

Father is subtly signaling for her to leave, but the Flashy Mammoth shows no sign of backing down. Finally sensing the tension, Panda and Éclair stepped in between them.

It looks like Keba Mammoth’s eyebrows twitched slightly at Panda’s words.

Kou is making it clear right here that he’s not going. I suppose Kou is worried about the elephant in his own way. All right, I’ll have to do my best, too. I’ll send a subtle signal to Father with my eyes.

Just as Kebamammoth was about to open the door and step out, I went into stealth mode and followed right behind my Father and the others. Perhaps Kebamammoth wasn’t interested in anyone but my Father, because even though I’d vanished from the spot, he didn’t even notice.

It seems there are some surprisingly capable creatures out there. This is quite a hassle. If it were a Rival, I’d probably be able to fly past without being noticed.
I’ve got no choice, so I’ll go with the “Flying Mode”—a candidate for my third form that’s still under development. I’ll use my spear to create a Windmill, spin at high speed, and float through the air as I move. Of course, I’m using Magic to cancel out the sound of flight and the wind pressure.
Flutter, flutter, flutter!

It’d also be easy if the entire clan suddenly went missing. As for the evil factions exploiting my Father, the only solution is to eliminate them.
Come to think of it, when I first started the loop and arrived in Siltvelt, I probably should have looked for anyone holding a suspicious meeting and taken them out. Siltvelt isn’t exactly united, after all. Eliminating them secretly without leaving any evidence might be an effective strategy. After all, someone from the Mammoth clan might have been mixed in among those at the meeting. It might have killed two birds with one stone.

“Hmm…”
Well, I suppose I can resolve this without going that far.
“It’ll be fine! Zou will definitely tear this house to shreds!”
There’s not much for me to do, really. Or maybe I should storm into Zou’s place and spout some passionate, high-sounding nonsense like I did to the pig? Zou is a great guy, and I do like him, but could I really express my affection with the same passion as I did back then?
……I don’t think so. Now that I’ve awakened to true love, Filo-tan is number one for me. I think I could say the same thing to my Father, but what’s the point of trying to win Zou over? This might actually be a job best left to Father. Or maybe I should leave it to Kou.

I have a hunch that Kou’s feelings for Zou are about the same as those of Big Sister and her friends. Let’s try asking Kou about it in a roundabout way.

“Hey, there’s this guy named Elmero who’s been whispered to by that guy and looks like he’s about to go on a rampage…”
“I-I hope he’ll be all right… And please stop insulting Elmero-sama.”
“Thanks for the info. Well then, I’ll be off!”
I’ve gathered all the intel I need. I’ll briefly go into stealth mode and resume my movement.
“H-he’s gone!”
“I haven’t gone anywhere. I heard what I needed to hear, so I’m just heading back.”

And so, having concluded my exchange with the rat Beastmen and their slaves, I returned to the room where Kou and the others were holding down the fort.

Rival, you bastard! What on earth are you doing here?!

I’ll prioritize wiping my Rival off the face of the earth before fighting my Father! But if I unleash Brionac at full power, stray shots will hit the others. So, I’ll focus on a single target! This is a sure-hit attack!

Ugh… Those are such cold, dismissive words from my Father. Does he care that much about my Rival!? That guy is a dragon—he’s my enemy! With an attitude like this, Filo-tan and Sakura-chan will be heartbroken!
…No, my faith in my Father is whispering to me. That he’s deliberately protecting my Rival. That he’s making me angry to minimize the damage—so that Filolial-sama’s egg won’t be broken because of me.
I do have faith in him. But I’m also angry. That’s exactly why I can’t show any mercy!

“Hah! This is—”
My father, anticipating what would come next after my thrust, deflected the tip of my spear with his shield.
“Burst Lance X!”
With a loud bang, the tip of my spear exploded with extraordinary force.

Even my father, impressive as he is, took a hit from my Burst Lance attack and was wounded, but he immediately healed his injury with Magic.

My rival and Yuki-chan are locked in a grapple, but right now we should focus our attacks on Father.
“Boo-boo-boo-boo!”

“Turn into a pile of charcoal with this! Brionac X!”
I fired my very first Brionac aimed at Father, as if I were praying.
“Air Strike Shield V! Second Shield V! Shield Prison V! Shooting Star Shield X!”
With loud clangs, my Father took my attacks head-on. In this world, my Father usually deflects attacks with moves like Air One-Way Shield, but this time, he’s taking them head-on to keep the Brionac’s trajectory from veering off course. What’s more, he’s adjusting his Defense Power to make it look like the skill shields that appear are getting shattered one after another. Ugh… Even from a vantage point like this, I can really feel my Father’s compassion and acting skills.
“Woooooooooooooo!”
Screaming, I keep attacking my Father without putting any real power behind my strikes. I destroy the shields that Father summons one by one… After breaking the Shooting Star Shield barrier, the shield cage shatters, and just as I’ve penetrated it slightly, I run out of ammo and catch my breath, panting heavily.
“Haa… haa… He’s so tough.”
“That’s… exactly what I was going to say.”
Guh… I must have gone too hard—my Father looks like he’s injured. How should I fight from here on out?
“Hate Reaction! Come on, come at me!”
My Father cast a skill that draws enemy aggro right at me. Guh… For some reason, I just can’t stop focusing on my Father.
“Bububu!”
Now those pigs are even launching attack Magic and sniper fire at us! Just how far do they plan to take this?
“Guh…”
“I’m not just going to stand by and watch!”

“Naofumi!?”
“Motoyasu-sama!”

Just as I was thinking that, a loud thud echoed from the distance!
This must be—! It seems that while we were buying time, Zou and Kou must have discovered something. They’ve apparently cleared a wide escape route.

num: 925
title: Special Edition: I Reincarnated as the Villainous Princess of *The Shield Hero*—What Do You Think I Should Do?
date: 2019/04/01 10:00

When I came to, I found myself alone in a luxurious room. Where… on earth… am I? Unable to make sense of the situation, I looked at the vanity nearby.
But what I saw there wasn’t my own familiar face… no. This face was unmistakably that of the villain known as Vitch—the root of all this trouble.
Vaguely, I recall a past life…?　I should have been working as an office lady in modern society.
My name was… what was it again? I can’t quite remember. However, there’s no doubt that the woman reflected in this mirror is the foolish and utterly wicked princess who appears as an enemy in *The Rise of the Shield Hero* and *The Spear Hero’s Redo*.
*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. A work that began as a serialization on the “Let’s Become Novelists” website, was later published in book form, and even adapted into an anime.
It’s the story of Naofumi Iwatani, a college student who came to the library to read, and who, while reading a book titled *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons* that he happened to find, is summoned to another world as the Shield Hero—the hero who saves the world depicted within the book. From this clichéd beginning, he becomes entangled in various conspiracies.
Starting with the other three Heroes—who can’t seem to shake their “video game” mentality—the story follows Naofumi as he fends off conspiracies and false accusations orchestrated by Melromarc, the summoning nation that seeks to persecute him because, from a religious perspective, he is the Shield Hero of an enemy nation. I’ve been reading this series since I was in high school. It’s a work that divides readers—some see it as unconventional yet classic, while others view it as classic yet unconventional—and many find it stressful to read.
After *The Rise of the Shield Hero* concluded, the author wrote a new side story titled *The Spear Hero’s Redo*. This story begins with the Spear Hero—who was portrayed as the main antagonist in *The Rise of the Shield Hero*—getting trapped in a loop in a parallel world. Even though he knows the future, the clumsy Spear Hero—whose personality has changed—tries his best to achieve his ideal future… well, not exactly.
It’s a story about him being infatuated with Filo, one of the heroines from *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, while regretting his past mistakes, struggling to help the Shield Hero, and doing his best to meet Filo. Since the Spear Hero—who’s pretty out there in his own way—tries to force his way through necessary steps, this story reveals events that couldn’t be fully depicted in the main series, *The Rising of the Shield Hero*.
I remember this well because I used to read and enjoy both of these stories a lot. I pored over the characters depicted in the novel’s illustrations and across various media. That’s exactly why there’s no way I could mistake her.
This woman—whose features could almost be called those of a beautiful girl when she puts on a innocent facade, but whose face, when she smiles defiantly, can only be described as that of a villain—is undoubtedly… the villainous princess who would later be known as Vitch. Why is she… that villainous princess?
I gaze at the mirror once more. Hmm, she really is a beauty. When she’s not making that villainous expression and just acting naturally… she doesn’t look entirely out of place as the heroine of a manga aimed at men… How does this even work? At the very least, I don’t think it’s the kind of face that gives her away as a villain at first glance. Well, maybe that’s necessary so the events in the original story make sense.
As I thought that, I looked out the window… and caught a glimpse of someone coming up the stairs. That’s… yeah, no doubt about it. It’s the Four Holy Heroes. I quietly opened the door and called out to the soldier on patrol.
“Excuse me.”
“Ha! What may I do for you, Lady Malty?”
The soldier, startled by my voice, saluted while trying to hide his fear. It seems I still hold some power here. Let’s confirm that, just to be safe.
“Could you tell me what’s happening in the castle right now?”
“Ha! Word has spread throughout the castle that, under the orders of the Three Heroes Church and Aultcray King, the Four Holy Heroes have been successfully summoned! Would you like to attend the audience?”
Just as I thought… it seems I’ve really ended up in another world—the world of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*. In fact, there’s even an option to bring up my status icon right in my field of vision…
“No, but… I plan to observe the situation from the back.”
If I recall correctly… the story went that this princess was actually hiding in the back of the throne room.
“I’m sorry for stopping you. Please return to your duties.”
“Ha!”
The soldier saluted and quickly left the scene. He’s probably talking behind my back right now. Well… to be honest, I’ve read quite a bit of the *Shield Hero* series, and it’s one of my favorite works.
It really fuels my ship-related fantasies, and I’m a big fan of the Faubrey arc featuring the Spear Hero… There’s no doubt I’m that kind of person.
My favorite pairing is Spear × Shield. The other way around is good too. I want to see these two interact.
My mind is racing enough that I’d like to take advantage of this opportunity to pull off all sorts of underhanded schemes… but at the same time, my situation in the *Shield Hero* series is extremely dire. After all, in this series, those who retain memories of their past lives are called “reincarnates,” and I was a pawn of the mastermind behind all the chaos that’s wreaking havoc on the world. So… if I make a wrong move, not only will I be killed, but my very soul might be erased.
Suddenly, I pinch my cheek to see if this is a dream, and a sharp pain shoots through me. Yeah… I really have been reincarnated as Vitch. No… I’ve been possessed by her, actually. This Vitch has all sorts of backstory—or rather, she’s a troublesome presence—and if I’ve been possessed by her, there must be all sorts of complications with her original self… but there’s no strange voice or anything.
…How am I going to survive from here on out? The world is experiencing a phenomenon known as “waves.” If we respond too casually to this crisis, not only will the country continue to fall into ruin, but the world itself might be destroyed. After all, the country is secretly stirring up discord among the Heroes, and it seems this country’s religion believes that after framing and killing the Shield Hero, the world will be saved by the Three Heroes.
Only followers of their own religion will be spared from the time of destruction. A new era will begin with the believers and Heroes who have overcome the crisis. When I look up the religious texts and teachings from the world of my past life, I find quite a few descriptions like that. I can imagine it’s a way to keep believers loyal, but the Three Heroes Church has actually put it into practice.
It may seem foolish, but apocalyptic theories are everywhere. I’m sure they existed in the world of my past life, too.
So, given this situation… what should I do?
Should I, as a “good guy” reincarnate, explain the situation to the heroes and try to get them to believe me? Something like, “I know everything about this story, so please trust me.” But… the moment I say that, if a bomb set by the mastermind behind the scenes were to explode, blowing my head to pieces and even obliterating my soul, that would be the end of the story.
Should I decide to be a bystander, do nothing, and keep my distance from the heroes? That’s not a bad option either. At the very least, if I do nothing, I might be able to avoid putting my own life in danger.
But… if I try anything strange… well. If I use my modern knowledge to do something unnecessary, it seems like ruin is bound to be my fate. There’s no doubt this is the kind of story world where getting too cocky will lead to nothing good.
It’s a bit of a meta way of thinking, though. Neither the Queen nor Princess Melty would complain if I just did nothing.
But… if I remember correctly, wasn’t the plot supposed to go something like this: I’d be made to take responsibility for the Hero’s summoning, and the Queen would end up proposing a marriage alliance with that sadistic King Faubrey…? The Queen is compassionate and wants to avoid marrying me off, but if King Faubrey makes a strong demand, there’s a non-zero chance she won’t be able to refuse and will end up offering me to him. It’s easy to imagine that the fact I was a companion of the Spear Hero was one of the reasons she was able to refuse the marriage proposal in the first place.
Taking action is dangerous; doing nothing is dangerous… Hmm. I need to strike a balance… while making sure the Queen doesn’t marry me off, and without provoking the Heroes… Escaping as a commoner or fleeing the country is probably out of the question—it’d be the work of the Shadow Organization or some covert unit. If I tried something like that, they’d suspect I’m up to something and might go ahead with the marriage anyway.
…It’s starting to feel like I’m in a pretty tight spot. Why did I have to end up as Vitch of all people? If I had to choose, I’d have preferred to be Melty or Raphtalia.
No, actually, maybe a background character—like Keel… or maybe someone low-key like Imiya would be better in this situation? But come to think of it, I’m pretty sure even those characters had pretty tragic pasts and circumstances. I don’t want to end up in a situation like that.
……It’s almost like I’m wondering, “Who would actually be a good choice?”…… that’s when it hit me. Elena, the Lazy Pig! If she manages to worm her way into the Hero’s good graces and just keeps an eye on his mood, she’ll be able to slip away safely. She doesn’t even have a particularly tragic backstory.
Or maybe Filo…? No, that’s a bit too much. Just think about it. If I, a modern-day office worker, were to go around saying, “Filo’s name is Filo!”—that would be problematic in so many ways. Besides, I don’t even know if I could reincarnate as a Filolial in the first place.
It would’ve been better if I’d been a mob Filolial raised by the Spear Hero! Long live reincarnation as a monster!
I unconsciously bit my nails, my teeth grinding. I looked every bit the villainess. With that, I quietly made my way to the audience chamber to peek in on the heroes’ audience.
I have a vague grasp of the castle’s layout from my memories as a princess, so I don’t get lost. I wonder how I should go about this? Since all sorts of people from other worlds have come to this one, it should be hard to make money or gain recognition using modern knowledge.
---
Just as I was thinking that, it suddenly—an idea occurred to me.
---
……Is this world I’ve been reincarnated into *The Rise of the Shield Hero*?
Or is it *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*?
---
If it’s the former, there are still plenty of possibilities waiting to be tapped. If I stay devotedly by the side of Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, especially regarding the king’s and the kingdom’s behind-the-scenes schemes, there’s a high chance things will work out.
It’ll be hard work, but the rewards will be great. The queen will appreciate me, so I can avoid being forced into marriage. The Shield Hero, whose personality hasn’t changed, seems to have a bit of an ulterior motive, but he comes across as a perfectly ordinary young man. He’s the kind of otaku who’ll understand if you just talk to him. He’ll believe me even if I hide my true feelings.
If I nurture him properly… yeah. There’s a high chance we’ll survive. As for the shadowy schemes behind the scenes, let’s leave that to the Queen to handle.
As for self-defense, as long as he has knowledge of the series, he’ll be fine. Since I’ve studied the backstory of *The Spear Hero* thoroughly, I’m sure we’ll manage somehow. Besides, there’s a suspicion that *The Shield Hero* comes from the world of a cooking manga, so I’m a little curious just how delicious his food is.
But… if it turns out to be *The Spear Hero* instead, that would be the worst-case scenario.
After all, in the *Spear Hero* reboot, the protagonist—the Spear Hero—basically can’t tell the difference between a woman’s voice and a pig’s squeal. What’s more, I’m considered the absolute worst pig of them all and am even called the “Crimson Swine.” To top it off, there’s a high chance he’ll try to kill me at the first opportunity.
You know… it feels like he’d just suddenly kill me out of the blue. Even if I’m not doing anything in particular, I could just be walking through the castle when suddenly, out of nowhere, a spear pierces my chest from behind and I die… that’s right, hahahaha… BAD END… that’s totally a possibility. It’s like there’s a 1% chance of a death roll every time I take an action, with no save function.
What do you call that? Like that guy in armor.
It’s a bit of a meta thought, but it seems plausible. It’s the kind of development where something happens in future chapters I haven’t read yet.
That’s because *True Spear*, the sequel to *The Spear Hero’s Redo*, hasn’t been completed yet. There might still be countless unexplored parts or landmines lying around.
Anyway… let’s first confirm which one it is. Judging by what happened earlier, he’ll definitely introduce himself during the audience. I quietly slip behind the throne room and prick up my ears.
“I am the king of this realm, Aultcray Melromarc the 32nd. Heroes, raise your heads!”
Ah, so this is the father of this body—the man who would later be called the “Trash King.” He was the “Hero of the Staff” and known as the “Wise King of Wisdom,” and apparently played a significant role in Melromarc’s past.
Nowadays, though… to put it mildly, he’s a “Madao.” He’s just a hopeless old man—or “Madao,” for short. He’s a troublesome old geezer who won’t come to his senses until he loses a few things. I think he’ll listen to me, his daughter, but when it comes to Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, there’s a high chance he’ll go off the rails. I hope he’ll stop just because I told him to… but since he didn’t seem to back down even after Melty tried to persuade him, it might be difficult.
As I was thinking about this, the king and his entourage began explaining the crisis facing this world.
“I get the gist. So, you’re asking us—who were summoned here—to work for free?”
“That’s a pretty convenient story, isn’t it?”
“We don’t owe you anything, do we? It’d be unbearable to work for free only to be told ‘goodbye’ once peace is restored. Actually, I want to know if there’s even a way for us to get back home—what’s the deal with that?”
“Guh…”
That’s when the Heroes secretly clenched their fists.
“We’ve also prepared financial aid. We truly want you, the Heroes, to protect the world, and we intend to provide a place for you to do so.”
“Don’t think you can keep us on a leash. We’ll cooperate as long as you don’t become our enemies.”
“…I suppose so.”
“Exactly.”
…… Yeah. This flow is definitely *The Shield Hero*. Good, good.
No… I’m starting to feel a little uneasy. If you ask me if I remember the details, I’m a bit iffy on this part of the exchange. But in terms of the flow… it’s definitely right, I think. I listen to the heroes’ self-introductions with my hands clasped together, as if in prayer.
“My name is Ren Amaki. I’m 16 years old and a high school student.”
Yeah, he’s got that shota vibe and is pretty cute. I think he’ll end up having the best personality. He’s the classic hero, isn’t he? Though the events after peace is restored do evoke a lot of sympathy.
But more importantly, what’s coming next!
Shield, shield, shield!
“My name is Motoyasu Kitamura! I’m The Love Hunter!”
It was a spear-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! I leaned against the wall, unable to help but feel despair at the death flags that were bound to appear from here on out.
What’s going to happen to my life—!?

“No. Absolutely not—we—”
“I get it, I get it. You just want to get rid of those hopeless parasites, don’t you? Do whatever you want.”
In that case, which side would the Pig King of Faubrey fall on? People say he’s pretty dangerous, but since we follow the “an eye for an eye” principle, my Father and I generally don’t get involved with him, right?

Let us join forces to develop the technologies of unknown worlds… so that foolish conquerors and evildoers known as ‘Tenseisha’ will never run rampant again!”
“I understand what you’re trying to say, but…”
Father turned his gaze toward me and my Rival. Well, yeah… we already resolved those kinds of issues back in our original world.

“Uh, yeah… I suppose so.”
The queen, having come to her senses, nodded as well.
“I thank the heroes from the other world and the Queen of Melromarc for their generosity!”
I guess that wraps things up for now, right?
“As for the requests, the Queen and I will handle them with each country. We can already sort a lot of it out based on what Ren and Itsuki—who are with you—have said… So, was it the Filolial Cross? As a sort of opening act, is that all you have to say?”

So Rival lamented. Apparently, it had something to do with the parallel world being created right after the world fusion. That was the situation, then. I had absolutely no idea.

“Bubu…”

Father is grumbling about what a troublesome process it all was.

The crisis is over, after all. For now, I suppose our role as heroes has come to a temporary conclusion.
“However, the scars left by the gods and the reincarnated ones still remain. This is both my atonement and my destiny… Sorrow will eventually breed conflict… Therefore, I must eliminate every spark of sorrow that remains for future generations.”
Well, my Father from the first world did defeat the Crimson Swine itself. But it seems he’s acting with the future in mind—after we heroes have saved the world. After all, there are indeed many people who were wounded by reincarnated individuals like Takt. Given that Trash himself was filled with deep hatred toward Demi-Humans and Beastmen due to the Crimson Swine’s underhanded schemes, it stands to reason that he’s trying to save those who are in a similar situation to his own. For now, I understand Trash’s resolve.
“And to build lasting peace, we need a presence that can bridge the gap between those with different ideologies and appearances.”
“…Is that what you call the Filolial Cross?”
“We are still immature… We cannot understand others as they are, and we end up fearing and hurting them… But one day, just as Tyran, his son, and Lucia did, I will make a world where we can trust one another a reality!”
Trash declared this with an intense gaze. With a gaze like that, he could probably brainwash someone. I can sense that level of incredible determination.
“So when I’m in this form, I want you to call me Filolial Cross, Captain of the Knight Order of the Divine Bird!”
With a click, Trash put his iron mask back on.

“Who asked you to say something clever!”

Most of the food-related things were already things Father had been making all along, and plenty of it has been recreated in this world too.

Those are the kind of things you’d only see around Faubrey or Shieldfreeden.
“So, about Fohl acting as the one to restrain Atla—what exactly happened there?”
“Apparently—in Father’s world, Tiger Girl turned out to be the daughter of some massive conglomerate, and she kept using her money to barge into Father and Big Sister’s life over and over.”
That much, I can easily imagine.
“I say, Motoyasu can easily imagine it, indeed. I’ve experienced school life with a wealthy pig more times than I can count.”
“Motoyasu-kun probably knows exactly how to deal with that kind of thing.”
“These days, if it gets truly bothersome, all it takes is a good verbal thrashing—but back when I was chasing after pig behinds, I was—well, utterly at their mercy.”
Thinking back on it now, it’s genuinely baffling why I ever put up with such a troublesome pig. There’s no doubt she was the type to sulk the moment things didn’t go her way. Come to think of it, back then… Father had been staring at me intently.
“There’s no point asking Motoyasu about this—it’ll probably just make things more troublesome.”
“Is something the matter?”
“Nothing. Just go look after the Filolials.”
If I had pushed my case a little harder back then, might I have gotten to visit Father’s world instead of Tiger Guy?
“The old Motoyasu-kun’s response to girls—well, pigs—was probably exactly as predictable as you’d expect… the type of soft-spoken guy who just silently takes a beating from some tsundere heroine, right?”
“Nowadays he’d probably retaliate without hesitation and beat them senseless.”
“We’d probably have to step in and stop him before things got recklessly dangerous.”
“Ha, pigs are creatures that resort to violence the moment things don’t go their way, I say. Sulk immediately and spread nasty rumors if you don’t apologize fast enough.”
I’ve heard plenty of times that she shows no mercy toward anyone who pulls that kind of stunt, myself included.
“Hypothetically, if I asked Motoyasu-kun for advice—like, ‘how should I go about persuading a runaway Atla-chan?’—what would you say?”
Hmm… so the premise is that it’s Father asking. If Father told me to do something about Tiger Girl, then… given that she’s the one who protected Father, Filo-tan, and Filolial-sama with her very life, I’d search for a way to restrain her while minimizing any injury, as much as possible. The complication is that the tiger girl of the first world existed as a translucent ghost-like being, so this only applies hypothetically, as if she were still alive. But assuming this is about Father wanting to resolve the matter—how would one deal with a tiger girl who keeps barging into the peaceful days shared by Big Sister and Father? Even when scheduling a date carefully in advance, that tiger girl has enough forcefulness and lack of self-control to crash right into Big Sister’s date day.
“Either let her do exactly as she pleases, or arrange for her to be constantly together with Big Sister at all times, I say.”
“……That’s basically just cutting her loose.”
“Enjoying a lively daily life through group activities is the correct answer, indeed. Whenever some event or gathering comes up, you go with whichever option Big Sister suggests.”
“Being nice to everyone while quietly raising the affection level of your favorite heroine—that’s the textbook definition of a gal-game protagonist.”
“Surely something will happen and she’ll suddenly settle down, or she’ll mysteriously stop appearing once another pig takes the spotlight.”
“That just sounds like ‘endure until you unlock the character-exclusive route’…”
For some reason, Father and the others let out a sigh. Whatever could be the matter, I wonder?

Itsuki spun the skewered suzu-kasutera around and around in protest—a rather memorable sight, I say. In the end, we managed to placate him by promising to make something once we’d finished clearing the dungeon, and so we pressed onward.

Sleeping Cat and Waking Bird
=====
That was a memory from a certain day, I say. It was an unremarkable day when Father, back when he was still the first Shield Hero, was tending to the monster stables in the village as part of his usual morning routine. I too was over in the Filolial stables next door, enjoying a refreshing morning.
“Ku… Kue.”
“Kue.”
The Filolial-samas suddenly grew restless, glancing all around, before all turning to face the same direction in unison. I was wondering just what had happened when—
“Naofumi-sama!”
Father had just stepped out of the monster stables when Big Sister’s voice rang out with unusual intensity, so I found myself heading outside as well, over toward where Father and the others were. The whole village was already up and about, looking forward to breakfast, and they too tilted their heads curiously at the sound of Big Sister’s voice as they watched the scene unfold.
“Ah… looks like we’ve got visitors,” Father muttered, sighing slightly, and set off walking beside Big Sister with a tired air about him.
“Ohh? Seems like something’s come up,” said Older Sister, who had apparently just gotten up despite drinking late into the night. She wasn’t even the least bit drunk, which put everyone nearby on edge.
“Is there some kind of problem, I wonder? Shall Motoyasu handle it, I say?”
“Motoyasu, you don’t need to do anything. There’s no real problem, so just behave yourself.”
“Understood, indeed!”
Father seemed to understand something about the situation. Looking for all the world like he was just heading out for a morning stroll, he walked ahead… toward the village entrance. Thud thud thud thud! The Filolial-samas all lined up together near the entrance, and Rival, for whatever reason, was flat on the ground on the other side, prostrating itself. And there, beyond them… stood a rounded, cat-like Demi-Human standing about a hundred and thirty centimeters tall, alongside a bird-type monster with dazzling plumage evoking crimson flames, its long peacock-like tail feathers trailing behind it. Looking more closely at the cat-like Demi-Human, it had a lizard-like tail covered in fur and was wearing overalls. Some traveler passing through the neighboring town, perhaps? From somewhere around Siltvelt? But judging by the reactions of the Filolial-samas, Rival, and Big Sister, that clearly wasn’t the case. Just what in the world was going on, I wondered?
“Rival, what exactly are you doing, I say?”
“Nano, shut up! Rival doesn’t have time to deal with you right now. Be quiet, nano!”
What a strange reaction. Ah! Look, over there’s a big Filolial-sama! It had the appearance of an ordinary Filolial, but it couldn’t fool these Motoyasu eyes, I say! Just as I was about to approach the large Filolial-sama, Kuu, Marine, and Midori stopped me.
“Mokkun, no!”
“I don’t think you should upset that person’s mood!”
“Goshujin-sama, I feel like you really shouldn’t upset that person’s mood.”
Filo-tan also approached Father, pointing at the bird-type monster beside the cat Demi-Human, warning him too.
“You’re seriously making everyone uncomfortable. Maybe tone it down a little, hm?”
“Nah, nah, I’m not putting off that much of a presence over here, am I? Ahh, this is a problem… I’m supposed to be the casual, laid-back type, you know.”
Somehow it felt exactly like royalty had shown up incognito among commoners—the cat Demi-Human and the bird monster seemed at a loss for how to respond, chatting between themselves.
“Ah, first off, everyone, don’t worry, I don’t have such a difficult personality that I’d get upset over something like this, so feel free to relax. If anything, I’m the one intruding here, just a visitor, that’s all.”
The bird monster spread one wing out like a hand, addressing the Filolial-samas reassuringly. At that, the Filolial-samas seemed to relax slightly, some of the tension draining from them.
“Right, right, ease up, everyone. Sorry for the sudden visit without any warning. We happened to run into an old friend nearby and figured we’d drop by to say hello while introductions were being made. Thought at the very least we ought to greet you properly. Oh, and that bird over there apparently just had something really good happen right before this, so it’s in an especially good mood—won’t get mad no matter what you do right now.”
“As long as your soul isn’t rotten, you can do whatever you like!”
The cat Demi-Human pointed at the bird monster, explaining this to Father. Did something happen if your soul was rotten? According to what Father said, apparently there was no one here with a rotten soul.
“And yet, both the dragon and the Filolials are on high alert regardless.”
“Raph…”
Raph-chan, perched on Father’s shoulder, cried out.
“Ah, that’s because of this troublesome bird here. Being the progenitor of all winged creatures, it’s letting off this bizarre aura without holding back at all. Quite the nuisance, isn’t it?”
“Being popular is a hard cross to bear… though you’re one to talk, letting your own presence leak out everywhere.”
“Mine’s fine because only certain beings can even sense it. Otherwise they wouldn’t notice at all.”
“…If you could hide it, you could’ve just taken that thing down yourself. And what’s with the ‘I was alone’ bit, huh?”
In response to Father, the cat Demi-Human answered with an easy, unbothered expression.
“The other side wasn’t stupid enough to fall for that, you know? Well, maybe they were a little stupid. Anyway, I really was alone back then. I’m not lying, and besides, you wouldn’t leave the fate of the world up to just anyone, would you?”
“Yeah, sure…”
The cat Demi-Human clapped its hands together with a small pop, shifting its gaze away from Father toward the rest of us standing behind him.
“Well then, allow me to properly introduce myself. To you all, I suppose I’d be what’s known as a god-hunter. My name is Ark. I had a bit of an encounter with Naofumi-kun here, and I ended up lending him a hand.”
“Yeah, that’s right.”
“Yes, we were saved by you back then.”
The one who had introduced itself as the cat Demi-Human, now revealed to be the god-hunter Ark, spoke thus. And Father and the others nodded along. So then, this was apparently someone Father owed a great deal to, from back when he was working to defeat the Crimson Swine’s true body. Father turned his gaze toward the bird monster standing beside Ark.
“You’ve probably already heard from Ark, but I’m Naofumi Iwatani. This is Raphtalia beside me. There are plenty of others behind us too, but introducing everyone would take forever, so if you want to talk to them later, go ahead.”
“Sure, sure. My name is… well, like him, I go by a lot of names, but I suppose I’m most often called the Phoenix. Not that I’m immortal or anything, mind you.”
“Well, it wouldn’t make much sense for a bunch of god-hunters to be immortal themselves.”
“Exactly. We just sleep and wake up, that’s all.”
“I mean, that’s not really a name though, is it?”
“I know, I know. There’s also ‘Hōō,’ but that already exists in this world too, doesn’t it? So for simplicity’s sake, just call me Hō—might end up being my next name anyway.”
Having said that, the bird monster who called itself Hō gave a small bow.
“Ah, I also happen to have the role of a god-hunter myself, though it’s different from this one here, who brings eternity to an end.”
At the mention of ending eternity, Hō pointed at Ark. So it had a title like that too, huh.
“Sometimes I’m called the progenitor of all winged creatures too, you know. World renewal is technically his… job, but don’t worry. This world isn’t so old or rotten that it needs renewing.”
It all sounded like quite a grand conversation—were these two on the same level as Ren or Black Thunder, I wondered?
“So you, who seems on par with that one, are you like some kind of dragon progenitor? You’ve got that sort of vibe about you.”

No blood relation, but a position like the clan chief’s brother-in-law… I see, that did paint a somewhat different picture, I say.
“Haaah…”

That was clearly code for “please leave already.” Even looking like that, it knew all about Japanese customs!

Ark stated this flatly. Now that I thought about it, this Ark fellow—I couldn’t sense anything from it at all, not even the faintest presence. Was this what being a god-hunter meant, I wondered?

“……”
“……”

“Don’t forget to subscribe to the channel!”
“It’d make me super happy if you left a like, ribbit!”

“Off we go, then!”
“Departure time!”
“Kuro-chan, keep this a secret from Ren, alright, I say?”
“Got it! Shadow Saint Hero’s awakened and Ren’s gonna play with us, right? I’ll invite Keel later too!”

“I mean, there’s no subscribe button or like button on this thing… who on earth taught Motoyasu-kun those video site catchphrases?”
In one smooth motion, Itsuki raised his hand, drew back his bow, and shot the video crystal clean through. It shattered into countless fragments and scattered into nothing.
“I had a feeling this might be the case… don’t you agree, Ren-san?”
“Yeah. If he’d done all that in that form and just kept quiet about it, I would’ve let it slide.”
“And yet here he is, provoking us like this even after we let it go… No matter what, we’re finding him and stringing him up.”
“Agreed.”
And with that, Ren and Itsuki burst out of my house and took off running.

The bird monster spread one wing out like a hand, addressing the Filolial-samas in reassurance. At that, the Filolial-samas seemed to relax just a little, the tension easing from their shoulders.
“Right, right, take it easy. Sorry for dropping by unannounced like this — we happened to run into an old friend nearby, and thought we’d swing by to say hello while making introductions. Figured the least we could do was greet you properly. Oh, and this bird here had something really good happen right before this, so it’s in a great mood — won’t get angry no matter what right now.”
“As long as your soul isn’t rotten, you can do whatever you want!”
The cat Demi-Human explained, pointing at the bird monster as it addressed Father. Did something happen if your soul was rotten? According to what Father had heard, there wasn’t anyone here with a rotten soul, apparently.
“And yet, despite that, both the dragon and the Filolials seem to be on high alert.”
“Raph…” Raph-chan, perched on Father’s shoulder, gave a little cry.
“Ah, that’d be this troublesome bird here. Being the progenitor of all winged creatures, it’s giving off this weird aura without holding back at all. Real nuisance, isn’t it?”
“Being popular is a heavy burden to bear… though you’re one to talk, leaking your own presence all over the place.”
“Mine’s fine because only certain people can even sense it. Otherwise they wouldn’t even notice, would they?”
“…If you could hide it, you should’ve just taken that thing down yourself. And what’s with the ‘I was alone’ bit, anyway?”
In response to Father, the cat Demi-Human answered with an easy, unbothered expression.
“The other side wasn’t quite that stupid, you know? Well, maybe a little stupid, actually. But yeah, I was alone that time. Not lying about that. Besides, you’re not the type to leave the fate of the world in someone else’s hands, are you?”
“Yeah, sure…”
The cat Demi-Human clapped its hands together with a pop, turning its gaze away from Father toward the rest of us standing behind him.
“Let me properly introduce myself, then. I suppose, from your perspective, I’d be what’s called a Godslayer. Name’s Ark. I had a little encounter with young Naofumi here, and lent him a hand.”
“That’s right.”
“Yes, we were saved that time.”
The cat Demi-Human, now introduced as Ark the Godslayer, spoke, and Father and the others nodded along. So then — this was someone Father owed a considerable debt to, in the matter of defeating the Crimson Swine’s true form. Father turned his gaze to the bird monster standing beside Ark.
“You’ve probably already heard from Ark, but I’m Naofumi Iwatani. This one here is Raphtalia. There’s a bunch more behind me too, but if we go through introductions one by one we’ll be here all day, so talk to whoever you like later if you want.”
“Sure, sure. My name is— well, like him, I’ve got a bunch of names, but I’m most often called the Phoenix, I guess? Though I’m not exactly immortal, mind you.”
“Well, folks who hunt down self-proclaimed gods being immortal would be something, huh.”
“That’s about the size of it. We just sort of… sleep and wake, that’s all.”
“I mean, that’s not really a name, is it?”
“I know, I know. Well, there’s ‘Phoenix’ too, and all that. You’ve got one of those in this world too, don’t you? So for simplicity’s sake here, just call me Ho — it’s close to what might end up being my next name anyway.”
So saying, the bird monster who called itself Ho gave a small bow.
“Oh, I’ve got a role as a Godslayer too, you know. Different from this one’s job of ending eternity, though.”
At the mention of “ending eternity,” Ho pointed at Ark. So there was that title as well, huh.
“Sometimes called the progenitor of all winged creatures too. World rebirth is his… job, but don’t worry. This world isn’t so old or rotten that it needs rebirthing.”
This all sounded like quite the grand scale of conversation — were these two on the same level as Ren or Black Thunder, perhaps?
“So you, being roughly on the same level as him, are what — the progenitor of dragons or something? You’ve got that kind of air about you.”
Father asked, looking over at Rival, who remained bowed low to the ground. So this was Rival’s point of origin, then! If that were the case, an enemy, I say!
“Hmm? Compared to the progenitor, I’d say I’m more like a sibling. The dragons just sort of consider me their boss, is all — it’s a bit different.”
“Sounds about the same to me.”
“Hmm… maybe think of it like an in-law sibling? Does that make more sense?”
No blood relation, but positioned as the sworn brother of the clan chief… I supposed I could picture that — definitely a slightly different position, I say.
“Haaah…” Father let out quite the weary sigh.
“Ah, you don’t need to look so troubled about it. It’d be a shame if you treated a visitor the way your world would with, what’s the phrase — serving bubuzuke tea as a hint to leave?”
A subtle way of saying “hurry up and go home,” I say. And to think, despite that appearance, it knew about Japanese customs!
“Well… I get it if you’re thinking ‘what now, took you long enough, you idiot!’ and feeling angry about it, but there are countless worlds out there, and it’s not like it’s fine — there were people actively preventing the warning signals from ever reaching us. Omniscience and omnipotence is nothing but arrogance anyway; it’s full of holes.”
Ark grumbled on rather thoroughly.
“While we’re staying here, I’ll at least let you vent your anger at me. You’ve more than earned that right. But, would you mind hearing our side of things, and the report, at least?”
“What is it?”
“The mastermind behind this whole affair — their world has already paid the price. No more waves will occur around here.”
Ark stated this flatly. Now that I thought of it, I’d just noticed — this person called Ark, I couldn’t sense a single thing from it, not even a trace of presence. Was this what being a Godslayer meant, I wondered?
“…I see.”
Father’s expression, which had remained flat through the report, finally softened with something like dissatisfaction.
“The one in charge tried making all sorts of excuses, but honestly, it was almost pathetic how they thought we wouldn’t dig deeper. That world had rotted through completely, root and branch. From their perspective, I’m probably nothing short of a mass murderer.”
Ark laughed as it said, “Well, whatever” — and for some reason, I felt like I’d seen that smile somewhere before.
“Anyway, that’s why we’ll be staying here a while, so take care of us.”
“Yeah, yeah. If you two are around, seems like troublesome sorts showing up will just resolve themselves without me lifting a finger. Just don’t slack off, though.”
“I know, I know. Gotta earn my keep somehow, right?”
Ho, having dismissed the Filolial-samas so they could relax and unwind as they pleased, joined back into the conversation. So then — the two Godslayers would be staying in the village for a while. The villagers, too, dispersed while chattering quietly among themselves. As for me, I wondered what to do — thinking of returning to my daily routine with the Filolial-samas — when Ho turned and looked at me.
“Ah, you — I recognize you. I remember now. You’re the one who made the news in that world I was in before, aren’t you? Motoyasu Kitamura, was it?”
“What? You know about Motoyasu?”
“I told you already, didn’t I? Before coming here, I spent some time in the world I was helping out — I remembered a little about him. Well, needless to say, he’s quite the celebrity. Woo-hoo, ladies’ man! Just like me!”
Father was glaring at me. Or rather, glaring at the spear more than me, it seemed. Something along the lines of: There was a Godslayer nearby and you didn’t even notice? Is your world really full of nothing but idiots like this? — I could practically feel Father’s thoughts radiating toward me.
“I-I don’t know anything about it, I say!”
“Well, no surprise you wouldn’t recognize me from back then. There was a lot going on with me at the time, you know. I’m all shining and glorious now, though!”
Seemed there was some kind of reason behind it. I didn’t know the particulars of Ho’s circumstances, but I was saved nonetheless, I say. Still, its sense of humor was… a touch cringeworthy. It felt a bit like watching my past self, giving me an itchy, uncomfortable feeling.
“…The news, huh.”
“Yep. Story was that he got killed in some crime-of-passion mess, but he ended up summoned to this world and avoided death that way… still some lingering traces of causal interference from this whole affair’s mastermind. I see, I see. Because he was killed, apparently all sorts of related parties went on a rampage, and the culprit met a rather gruesome end. Something about university— oop, that’s edging into someone’s privacy, not really my place to talk about it. Sorry ’bout that.”
So Ho seemed to be talking about matters related to my original world. Terribly irrelevant stuff, honestly.
“Oh? Trying to use his inherent nature to avoid ruin in an emergency, huh. I see, I see. Pure coincidence, but the fact that you and we ended up in the same world might’ve been some kind of causal connection after all.”
“Causal, I say?”
“Yep. Well, it’s something like your own nature, I suppose.”
This Ho person was saying things I couldn’t quite make sense of at all.
“…So Motoyasu, huh. Well, sounds like his ex from back home met a tragic end. Attempted murder-suicide, was it… no wait, if it was supposed to be a murder-suicide, but she still faced consequences… why is that?”
“Ended up too attached to her own life to go through with dying, in the end?”
“Pigs value their own hides above all else, I say. Drunk on the emotion of claiming to love me, no doubt, and once I was dead, it fled back to save its own precious self, I say.”
Pigs truly are a menace, I say! Ptooey! Indeed, I say!
“Well… even with some degree of interference, that particular part of a person doesn’t really change. She was pulled out of all those messy entanglements and summoned to this world instead — I’d say that actually worked out for the best, wouldn’t you?”
“…Motoyasu, do you have any wish to go back to your original world?”
“None whatsoever, I say. A world without Filo-tan and Filolial-sama holds no value at all, I say!”
“…There you have it. Good for you. Bird boss, I’d bet you’re about to become an object of worship for this guy too.”
“Ehh… you’re going to worship me? I get uncomfortable if people expect weird returns for that sort of thing, you know? Happens more often than you’d think.”
Was Ho a Filolial-sama or not, I wondered? I approached Ho to conduct my judgment. Sniff, sniff, I say.
“Wh-what are you doing?”
Hmm… somehow, it did seem to carry that same rich, fragrant scent found in Filolial-samas. …Though, now that I thought about it, it also somewhat resembled the scent I recalled from when we defeated the Phoenix. In that sense, the description of “boss of the Filolial-samas” wasn’t inaccurate at all. Phoenix… now that I thought of it, the actual Phoenix had shared similar characteristics too. That made sense, I say.
“Right then, Ho, was it. I hereby acknowledge you as a Filolial-sama, I say! Rest assured — I seek no returns whatsoever from a Filolial-sama, I say! From this day forth, you shall be Ho-kun. I shall love Ho-kun equally alongside all the rest, I say.”
“Hold on a second! Please don’t lump me in with a bunch who consider pulling carts the highest form of joy in life!?”
Here, Ho pointed accusingly at the cart-pulling Filolial-sama in protest!
“What manner of blasphemy is this, I say! The Filolial-sama who pulls the cart is the very pinnacle of existence, I say! Ho-kun! You simply haven’t noticed that instinct within yourself yet, I say!”
“No, no, no, absolutely not! If you try to make me pull a cart, I will get angry, you hear me!?”
The Filolial-samas watched Ho’s refusal of my proposal with what seemed to be genuine concern. There was no need to worry so — no Filolial-sama could truly resist their own instincts, I say.
“Motoyasu doesn’t get angry even at insults that seem to deny Filolials, so long as he’s already decided to accept the thing, huh.”
“I suppose you could call it thoroughness, or something like that…”
“Well, it’s exceedingly troublesome, but maybe that’s a good quality too, in its own way.”
In any case, it seemed the apparent boss of the Filolial-samas would be staying in the village for a while, I say.
“…In any case, seems Filolials as a species have a nature that makes them want to avoid trouble. Watching their boss warily from a distance, I suppose.”
“Seems that way.”
“So, about Ark, boss of the dragons…”
Father looked around and turned toward Ark, who was smiling pleasantly nearby.
“You said you’re a visitor here… any particular plans for what you’ll be doing?”
“Just came to deliver the report on the incident and introduce you to this troublesome bird here — no particular plans beyond that. Oh, but if there’s work you’d like done, I don’t mind helping, so just say the word.”
“Managing the territory… looks like you’ve got a lot going on. This cat-slash-dragon guy, you know, does dorm-mother type work and childcare stuff on a whim sometimes — pretty useful, actually. Since he’s offering, might as well put him to work.”
Ho pointed at Ark, explaining to Father. Dorm mother and childcare, was it? So this meant a high aptitude for housework and childrearing, then.
“Ahh, brings back memories.”
“Hoh… well then, might as well have you help with various things.”
“Sounds fine to me.”
As this conversation went on, Rival watched from a distance, brows furrowed.
“Whoa… it’s looking at you like you just proposed something terrifying. Like, ‘Aren’t you scared, putting a Godslayer who’s also the dragon boss to menial chores?’ sort of look.”
“Don’t worry about it. Isn’t it worse if we’re not allowed to do anything and just get treated as honored guests?”
“Yeah, fair. Feels like there’s some hidden catch to that, doesn’t it.”
I see. Having power or authority tends to invite suspicion, doesn’t it. Ho and the others must have had their own struggles too, then. Seemed even Godslayers had their fair share of troubles.
“So… Ho, what exactly can you do?”
“Hm? Want me to whip up some fried rice with my flames?”
“Motoyasu can handle that much just fine.”
“Oh really? I think my fried rice is pretty good, though… well, I can do plenty of things, not that I can’t, but maybe wait until you’ve got a full picture of what’s needed before deciding? Oh, and I don’t do any secret techniques or prophecy-type stuff, just so you know.”
“Wasn’t expecting any of that from the start, honestly… what kind of preemptive excuse is that supposed to be. Anyway, I was in the middle of preparing breakfast. If you can cook, help out.”
When Father requested Ark’s help, it nodded in response.
“Guess I’ll help out then. First, let’s figure out what kind of flavors people like around here.”
And with that, Ark rolled up its sleeves and headed off toward the kitchen with Father. So the two of them cooked together in the kitchen. Father, looking rather bothered, cut ingredients midair with careless efficiency.
“So this is the kind of flavor that’s popular here, huh — alright, this should work.”
Ark too, in the kitchen, sampled the simmering pot with practiced ease, helping with the stewing. It casually pinched seasoning between its fingers and tossed it in without a second thought.
“Ah, Naofumi-kun. Pass me some of that ingredient there.”
“Sure. Toss me some of what you’re cutting too.”
“Yeah.”
Tap! Father sent the ingredients he’d cut flying with practiced skill toward Ark, and Ark tossed them back with a similarly deft motion. The village’s kitchen assistants watched, dumbfounded, at the sight. Father and Ark were cooking in perfect sync, exchanging ingredients back and forth. There was no room to step in between them, I say — jump in carelessly and you’d likely get hit by flying ingredients from both directions. This wasn’t on the level of mere “practiced hands,” I say. I could see now what Ho meant about the dorm-mother business. And so, before long, the cooking was finished and breakfast was set out before us.
“Bro, the food’s amazing again today! Which one’s the dish Ark-san made?”
“This one right here.”
When Keel asked, Ark had apparently made the soup. It fell short of Father’s slow-simmered, all-night soup, but personally, I thought it tasted quite good, I say. A somewhat richer flavor, more suited to modern tastes.
“Ohh! So this is the one Ark-san made!”
“That’s right. Haven’t quite matched it to the local flavors yet, though. If anything, it’s seasoned more for you modern folks — Naofumi-kun and the rest — rather than for the local palate.”
“Well, if you’re asking about my personal preference, this one’s spot on. Fairly versatile seasoning, I’d say.”
“Cooking’s all about individual preference, after all. Adjusting it to match the person eating is half the fun of it… but if you suddenly serve exactly what someone likes right off the bat, wouldn’t that kind of freak them out?”
“…Yeah, true enough.”
Father agreed with Ark’s remark. Indeed, Father was quite skilled at recreating flavors he already knew. Apparently he understood that if he immediately achieved a perfect recreation on the first try, it might come across as unsettling.
“Dunno exactly what’s going on, but this is tasty in its own way!”
Keel munched away, commenting on the food Father and the others had made.
“Hey, hey, Ark-san, you travel all over fighting off bad guys who show up in this world and stuff, right?”
“I suppose that’s how it’d look from your perspective.”
“So tell us about your travels!”
Keel asked Ark with remarkable familiarity.
“Hold on a sec — what about me!? I travel too, you know!”
Ho-kun asserted itself at this point.
“The journey… of life, you mean.”
“You’re a bird.”
“……”
Father and Ark looked at Ho-kun with the exact same expression. Their faces practically read “what an annoying creature.” Well then, allow me to ask instead.
“Ho-kun, tell me all about it, I say!”

The future branches off in countless directions, after all. And it’s painful not being able to choose the path you want, right when you want it. That’s how Ark answered—sounding, for all the world, like someone discussing college entrance exams.

It was true that I had been shallow, and without properly investigating anything, I had challenged Father to a duel.

Even Ark said it was the Crimson Swine, who had used me to the fullest, that was to blame. But that wasn’t good enough, indeed. My sin was that I had trusted the wrong person.

That… could it be referring to becoming immortal, I wondered? I recalled hearing from some pig or another that drinking a phoenix’s blood grants immortality. From the sound of it, it seemed both Hou-kun and this woman of his had similarly saddled Ark with the power of immortality. As Father and the others chatted amongst themselves, I kept piecing together the puzzle, intent on restoring the inscription—when suddenly, it gave off a faint glow. This was… surely something worth reporting—and just as that thought crossed my mind, the contents of the text left me utterly speechless.
You who make this text shine—I leave this for you, who have heard the chaos cat and the phoenix speaking of me. Should you report this now, the future you desire shall not come to pass. The one you believe in, the messenger from the heavens, and your happiness shall all draw nearer to ruin.
That was the sentence that first came into view.

“……”

Feeling a little uneasy about how thin it seemed, I wondered if that was just my ingrained poor-man's instincts talking. Like some tourist stashing cash before a trip abroad, I quietly hid about thirty silver coins inside my shield. Yeah. Somehow that made me feel a bit more at ease.
Quite a day it had been. I'd thought I'd try fighting alone for once, so I went out to the meadow and beat up a monster called a Balloon. So this is what it felt like to defeat a monster, huh. Though "popping a balloon" was really the only way to describe it. I sat down on the bed, then just lay back. An unfamiliar ceiling above me—same as yesterday—reminded me: I really had come to another world.

Pyon? What a strange way to end a sentence. Wondering about that, I opened the door, and there was... no one there?
