“The Shield Hero-sama said, ‘The night's not over yet,’ and came at me, trying to force my clothes off—”
The unfamiliar woman behind Itsuki pointed at me, weeping, condemning me.
“I got so scared... I screamed and ran out of the room for dear life and went to Itsuki-sama for help.”
“Huh? Seriously, who ARE you?”
What was going on? Last night, after chatting briefly with the visiting Usaunny, I'd slept soundly and had absolutely no memory of anything like this.
“Liar! Then why is Kanan-san crying so much!”
“No, seriously, who is that woman! And more importantly, where did you get that chainmail?”
“Ah, yesterday, while we were all having drinks, Kanan-san showed up at the tavern. After drinking together a while, she gave me this chainmail as a gift.”
That chainmail was unmistakably mine, however you looked at it. So this woman had apparently stolen my property and gear while I slept, then gifted it to Itsuki? There was no point reasoning with Itsuki here. I'd bring this to the king instead.
“That's right! Your Majesty! While I was sleeping, this thief stole everything I owned except my shield! Please, arrest that woman!”
“Silence, scoundrel!”
The king dismissed my plea outright.
“Forcing intercourse upon an unwilling citizen of my kingdom is an unforgivable act of savagery—were you not a hero, you would be executed on the spot!”
“I keep telling you, it's a misunderstanding! I didn't do it!”
But everyone present had already decided I was guilty and was proceeding as if it were fact. I felt the blood drain right out of me. What was this? What the hell was this?! Why was I being condemned for something I had absolutely no memory of doing? Gaping like a fish, I glanced at the thieving woman—thinking no one was watching—she stuck her tongue out at me, mocking me. That's when it hit me. I glared at Itsuki. I felt something dark and ugly welling up from the pit of my stomach.
“You! Don't tell me—you framed me for this just to get my starting funds and equipment!”
Pointing at Itsuki, I shouted with a volume that even surprised me.
“Ha! Listen to the sex criminal talk.”
“Don't screw with me! You were after my money from the start, weren't you—coordinated this whole thing to spread the equipment around to your buddies!”
Using someone else's woman-companion to pull off a stunt like this, all to steal my money. Whoever spoke first wins, huh, you bastard!
“To think you'd do something like this to a companion, even after coming to another world—how despicable.”
Ren delivered his cold judgment against me. What was with that composed, detached look on his face?! Look at the situation properly, damn it!
“Indeed. I don't think there's any room for sympathy either.”
Ren and Itsuki condemned me without a shred of hesitation. So that was it... these two had been in on it from the start. Because I had the shield, because I was weak, because I wasn't strong—they'd decided to kick me while I was down, to tilt things in their own favor even a little.
—Filthy. Nothing but cowardly, rotten scum, through and through. Come to think of it, this whole kingdom had never once tried to trust me from the very beginning. Who cared! Why should I protect people like this? Let it all burn! This whole world.
“...Fine, whatever. Just send me back to my own world already, why don't you. Go summon a new Shield Hero!”
Another world? Ha! Why should coming to another world make me feel like this?!
“Running away the moment things get inconvenient? How pathetic.”
“Indeed. Failing to properly fulfill your duties, and trying to force yourself on a woman besides...”
“Get out, get out! We can't keep someone who'd do this as a fellow hero, I say!”
I glared daggers at Ren, Motoyasu, and Itsuki as they spouted their self-serving nonsense, murder in my eyes. This was supposed to be a fun new world. And these bastards had ruined it. For some reason, Usaunny's face flashed through my mind. Was this the "painful experience" it had meant?
“There! Send me back to my own world already!”
At that, the king crossed his arms and groaned.
“I would love nothing more than to send a hero like you back immediately, but there is no method to do so. The researchers say re-summoning is only possible once all the heroes are dead.”
“...Wh-what did you say?”
“No way...”
Only now did Ren and Itsuki look flustered. Motoyasu just stood there silently glaring at me. There was no way back to my own world?
“You mean I can't even go home like this!”
Are you kidding me?!
“How long are you gonna hold onto me, huh!”
I roughly shook off the knight restraining me.
“Hey! Are you planning to resist?”
“I'm not attacking anyone!”
One of the knights punched me. Thwack! Nice solid sound. But it didn't hurt or even itch. The knight, on the other hand, apparently didn't feel the same way, clutching his fist and grimacing in pain.
“So? Your Majesty, what's my punishment supposed to be?”
I asked after swinging my arm around to shake off the numbness.
“...As things stand, since you exist as a countermeasure against the Waves, you bear no formal crime. But your crime has already become known throughout the kingdom. That is your punishment. Do not expect to be employed anywhere in this country.”
“Ohh, how very generous of you!”
So basically, level up as an adventurer and prepare for the Wave, huh.
“You will be summoned for the Wave in one month's time. Criminal or not, you are the Shield Hero. You cannot escape your duty.”
“I know that! I'm weak, remember? I don't have time to waste!”
Just as I noticed the jingle of the silver coins hidden in the back of my shield—
“Wait, I say.”
Here, Motoyasu, as if suddenly transforming into an overzealous soldier, grabbed my collar and shoved me back.
“Ow! Motoyasu, what are you doing!”
Looking at his face... what the hell was this guy doing? Was he coughing up blood? I wiped at a faint trickle of blood at the corner of his mouth.
“This punishment is far too lenient. I shall administer the punishment you truly deserve, indeed.”
“Oho! As expected of the Spear Hero, Kitamura-dono!”
“What are you planning to do?”
“……”
Motoyasu held his hand out toward me as I sat sprawled on the ground, and began chanting a spell.
“The Spear Hero, source of power, commands it. Unravel the workings of all creation once more, and transform this one's form.”
“Four Fairy Morph!”
Before I could even process the strange words, some kind of light gathered around Motoyasu and shot straight at me.
“Waaaaaaaaah!?”
With a poof and a puff of smoke, my vision switched in an instant.
“Th-this is...”
“Well I never...”
“Ohh...”
For some reason, Motoyasu and the others suddenly looked huge. What had they done to me? Looking down, I saw my body had gone strange—my hands had changed into something not human at all, and there was something like fur covering my belly. And further down, right in front of me... a beak!? Motoyasu's giant hand came looming toward my face and I tried to flee in a panic, but with such short legs I couldn't even get up before he grabbed me by the back.
“What is this!? What did you do! Hey! Motoyasu! What did you do to me?!”
“As punishment, you shall spend your days in that form! Fuhahahaha! Now get out of the castle, I say!”
With that, Motoyasu grabbed me, carried me outside the castle, and hooked me on the tip of his spear before hurling it.
“Gungnir!”
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
With a whoosh, I was carried off by the spear Motoyasu had thrown, flung high into the sky, sailing on and on endlessly. In no time at all I went flying—and with an impact like slamming into the ground, my consciousness cut out.
---
“——I need you to wake up, pyon.”
“Ugh...”
Regaining consciousness, I opened my eyes to find Usaunny shaking me, a blue sky behind it.
“Where am I...”
I could hear the crash of waves. Was the sea nearby?
“Are you alright, pyon?”
“Ah, yeah... you're Usaunny, right?”
“That's right, pyon. Nao—er, Naofumi-kun.”
Come to think of it, this Usaunny seemed to stumble over its words every time it tried to say my name, didn't it? Shakily, I felt around my face and body with my hands to check what had happened to me. But there was just something like fur, and I couldn't tell much. As I looked around, wondering what had become of me, Usaunny held out a hand mirror, and I took it to check. Reflected there was... a penguin wearing a Santa hat.
“What the hell is this?!”
“It seems Oto—Naofumi-kun has become a peckul, pyon.”
“A peckul?!”
“That's right, pyon. Apparently that's a type of creature, pyon.”
“I-is that so...”
Even being told that, there was no way I could accept this situation!
“That bastard Motoyasu! What did he do to me?! Was that magic or something?!”
Damn it... turning me into this shape out of nowhere—what was the meaning of this?! How was I supposed to turn back? No, actually—wasn't this shape closer to that of a monster?
“Where is this place?”
Looking around, I could tell this was some kind of abandoned village.
“Melromarc Kingdom, Seaetto Territory, Lulolona Village, pyon. It became abandoned due to damage from the first Wave, pyon.”
“I see...”
Looking closely, I could make out traces of monster claw marks and bones and other signs of damage. So a disaster of that magnitude really did exist...
“What on earth happened, pyon? I want you to tell me the circumstances, pyon. I'll lend you my strength, pyon.”
Since Usaunny asked me about the circumstances, I explained everything that had led up to me becoming a peckul.
“That sounds terrible, pyon. No matter what, I will lend you my strength, pyon.”
Hearing that, my heart felt somewhat lighter, in a way. It had said it wanted to help even before I'd fallen into such misfortune, and it believed my current situation. Just that alone was enough to lift me out of feeling like I had no one on my side. Still... I couldn't help but think this world wasn't worth saving.
“Ah... that helps. By the way, something's bothering me...”
Looking at Usaunny's appearance, it struck me—there were a lot of similarities between the small animal wearing a Santa hat and myself.
“I also had my form changed by magic, just like Oto—Naofumi-kun, pyon. The only way to return to your original form is to clear your name of the false charges and have the caster undo it, or to find another way to break the spell, pyon.”
“I see.”
So this Usaunny was also a victim of Motoyasu's, huh. At the time, I just took this at face value without particular suspicion. Later, I'd end up screaming at it, calling it a con artist, but that's a story for another time.
“Looking like this, and falsely accused too—there's no way I can gather companions and get strong... Usaunny, what about you?”
Setting the false charges aside, was there really anyone out there who'd help a guy who looked like a penguin? No way, right? The very idea of being a hero in this state was a joke.
“Due to the effects of the curse, I would hinder Na—Naofumi-kun's growth, so I can't fight alongside you, pyon.”
Tch! So the same restriction that keeps heroes from fighting alongside each other applies here too, huh.
“But I can help you in other ways, pyon.”
“Such as?”
“I'll buy up the goods that Na—Naofumi-kun gathers and sell them, pyon. I think I can sell things much better than Naofumi-kun, given how notorious your name has become, pyon. I'll also bring various other supplies for you to buy, pyon.”
“So basically you're saying you'll act as a merchant and handle things in my place?”
“That's right, pyon.”
“I see...”
Given that Usaunny was under a similar curse, I couldn't very well demand any more from it than that. Just having its help was better than nothing, I supposed.
“I'll also teach you all sorts of knowledge I've gathered about the Legendary Weapons, pyon. If you master how to use that shield's powers properly, you could become far stronger than the other heroes, pyon.”
“That helps. For now... I need food, money, and to level up...”
Whatever else, nothing would start without leveling up. But my stats hadn't changed much even after becoming a peckul. If anything, had I gotten weaker? My level hadn't gone up, at least. If there were any Balloons around, I'd love to punch something and grind some experience. I was itching to take my frustrations out on something. But with this body, I was slow, and punching wouldn't do much anyway. For now, I took out the silver coins I'd hidden inside my shield and showed them to Usaunny.
“Is there anything I can buy with this?”
“Plenty of things, pyon. Let me show you the list, pyon.”
Usaunny showed me a list of goods it could procure. ...Written clearly in copper and silver coin values, which helped a lot. It could even buy fish and such from me for resale. A pretty handy merchant, this one.
“If I can find some cooking equipment usable in this abandoned village, life shouldn't be too hard to manage... For now, might as well dive into the sea. I am a penguin, after all.”
“I'll go find some medicinal herbs and the like, pyon.”
“Alright, see you later.”
With that, I waved to Usaunny and dove into the sea.
---
Hmm... oh, as expected of a penguin, I could swim through the water exactly as I imagined. There were fish in the sea, and I could catch them easily. Fish I'd never seen in Japan, but I caught a few anyway, went back to shore, found a basket in the abandoned village, and stored them there. When I put some in my shield too, a new shield unlocked. Since it came with effects like improved fishing quality, I switched to it right away.
“I can just keep on swimming and swimming...”
As I swam, probably due to damage from the Wave, I spotted decomposing corpses on the seafloor here and there, which was pretty chilling. Further down in the depths swam monsters I clearly couldn't beat. For now, I figured I should focus on leveling up by fighting weaker fish-monsters found in the shallows.
“And then...”
After securing a decent amount of fish, I went ashore and decided to explore the area around the village. And then...
“Oh...?”
Some kind of adventurer or traveler with animal ears sprouting from their head noticed me. I braced myself somewhat warily, when—
“……”
They dashed straight at me, scooped me up, and started running.
“What are you doing! Let go!”
“…………”
Dash, dash, dash! Wasn't this person trying to kidnap me!? Worse, they stuffed me into a sack and tied it shut. Being suddenly kidnapped—what was going on?! I couldn't tell the difference in this world between monsters and people with animal ears, but given my current form was closer to a monster than a demi-human, was I being captured alive as a "talking monster"?!
“Guah!?”
As I thrashed about struggling, I took a heavy blow and lost consciousness.
---
“Mufufu... Father's captivating belly, pyon...”
When I came to, Usaunny had its face buried in my stomach. What was it doing? Was the texture of penguin fur really that comfortable?
“Are you alright, pyon?”
Pulling away with an innocent expression, Usaunny said this as if nothing had happened. It seemed to intend to pretend the previous action never occurred. Looking around, I saw we were back in the abandoned village.
“Nao—Naofumi-kun, you were nearly kidnapped, pyon. I managed to save you somehow, pyon.”
“Th-that's a relief, thanks.”
“Are you really okay, pyon? If you don't like it, please leave it to me, pyon.”
“Even so, I can't just keep relying on you for everything.”
“Please leave it to me, pyon. If I put my mind to it, I could bring peace to the whole world all by myself, pyon.”
Usaunny puffed out its chest proudly, but the sight was anything but reassuring. ...Later I'd find out it really could do exactly that, and end up kicking it for it, but that's beside the point.
“Damn it... seems like I might get caught and sold off as some kind of rare beast.”
Whether human or demi-human, I needed to be very careful around people from now on.
“...I could escape into the sea, at least. Guess I'll just have to focus mainly on the ocean.”
And so, with Usaunny bringing various goods and giving me a daily report of sorts, we settled into a routine. When Usaunny sold off the fish I caught, today's earnings came to about three silver coins.
---
A few days later.
“Haah...”
What was I supposed to do about this bizarre penguin-transformation, fish-catching lifestyle I'd fallen into? Fortunately, thanks to Usaunny teaching me how to reinforce my shield, I'd become sturdy enough to take hits from deep-sea monsters without flinching, but if I couldn't deal any damage back, that didn't get me anywhere. At best, salvage work and catching weak fish seemed to be the extent of what I could manage.
“I've brought some goods for troubled Father, pyon.”
At some point, Usaunny had started calling me "Father." Apparently I resembled its parent somehow.
“Piyo!” “Piyo!”
And somehow, riding on top of Usaunny's head were a white and a yellow baby bird—chicks that looked like the young of some carriage-pulling monster, like a certain famous yellow chocobo-esque creature.
“What in the world did you bring back this time?”
“Reinforcements to help troubled Father—slaves, pyon.”
“Slaves, you say... You've got such a fancy, cutesy look about you, but the stuff you bring back is way too heavy, man.”
“Then allow me to introduce them, pyon.”
This guy said it with a completely natural expression, like it was nothing at all. And so, guided by Usaunny, I was led to one of the houses in the abandoned village.
“First, Entry Number One! I believe she's a raccoon-species young lady, pyon. Extremely weakened, and she suffers from panic attacks where she screams in her sleep.”
“Cough, cough... um, where is this...”
“As it turns out, she's originally from this very village, pyon.”
The person Usaunny led me to was a girl with tanuki ears and a tail. She looked incredibly timid—no way she could fight. And on top of that, she seemed to have a cold. The stiff, frozen expression on her face gave off an unsettling vibe.
“Entry Number Two! That young lady's friend! Also extremely weakened. I've administered first aid, but caution is advised, pyon.”
“Haah... haah... cough cough...”
And this one was, by any measure, a girl weakened by illness. This one was seriously, genuinely not okay. Give her medicine and let her rest!
“Who are you...”
Even if I said I was the Shield Hero, there was no way she'd believe me, and right now I was some mysterious creature called a peckul anyway. Explaining the situation was way too much of a hassle, but what was I supposed to do? And more importantly, Usaunny—choose your merchandise better! There had to be a limit even to human trafficking.
“Just remember me as a peckul for now. I can't promise I'll be much help, but... I can't just abandon you either.”
“And Entry Number Three! A blind tiger-eared girl, unable to walk, suffering from an inherited incurable disease, pyon!”
“Uuu...”
And this one was wrapped head to toe in bandages. Usaunny... just what exactly do you expect from me? What am I supposed to do bringing me sick slaves who'll never be any use in a fight?! But abandoning them was harsh too, damn it! Are you trying to bankrupt me or something?!
“...I sense someone with a very strong, gentle presence, but... I suppose that means I've been disposed of separately from Onii-sama. Good. At last, Onii-sama can be freed of me...”
She looked like she might die at any moment. Seriously dangerous-looking, and there was no "Onii-sama" anywhere in sight.
“Hey, Usaunny.”
Beckoning it outside the building, I poked Usaunny with my flipper.
“What's supposed to be useful about those three? They're all half-dead!”
The raccoon-species girl, at least, seemed the most functional of the bunch, but the other two were bedridden.
“It's fine, pyon. If Father catches fish and gives them to them, they'll recover quickly, pyon. But slow, bad-tasting fish won't work, pyon. They'll waste away and die, pyon.”
“What kind of old man from the sixth entry of some legendary fantasy game are these kids supposed to be raised by!”
So catching fast fish and feeding it to them would make them healthy and useful as fighters, huh? Sure, it's an RPG cliché that weak characters joining your party have high growth rates, but was that gimmick supposed to actually make these three combat-capable? Shouldn't we be talking about herbs or expensive medicine just to keep them alive at this point?!
“I'll handle registering everyone's slave crests, so Father just needs to focus on catching plenty of fish and bringing them to me, pyon.”
“You, seriously... haah...”
Guess I had no choice but to just go along with it. I'd thought this whole world deserved to burn over that false accusation, but thanks to Usaunny, life itself was somehow manageable, and it kept saving me whenever I was about to get captured by humans. It was buying all sorts of things with the money too—right now was the groundwork phase; I needed to build up as much of an environment as I could before the next Wave hit. Thinking that, I went out fishing again that day and handed the catch to Usaunny, and sure enough, the enslaved girls gradually started to recover. The raccoon-species girl, Raphtalia, screamed at night just as Usaunny had said, and calming her down was quite the ordeal. Still, thanks to her friend Rifana getting a bit better, work around the village started going smoothly. It turned out she really was originally from this village, and she diligently worked hard on the village chores. And so, a little over a week had passed since I'd become a peckul...
---
That day, as I was swimming in the sea...
“Huh...?”
I noticed a mysterious black-and-white shadow far out in the water rushing toward me in an instant. Then I realized the shadow was that of an orca, and a certain memory surfaced in my mind. The natural enemy of penguins: orcas.
“Hi—”
I'd let my guard down, since even though I was slow on land, I could move quickly in the water. But no matter how you looked at it, this thing was far faster than me, and huge to boot. It could easily thrash me around and eat me. No, wait—with my reinforced shield, I should at least be able to outrun it! I've got to flee! Turning my back, I tried to make a full-speed escape, but—
I got grabbed. ...Grabbed? How? Turning around, I realized this orca had hands and feet attached to it!? Don't tell me—an adventurer in the water!?
“Damn it! Let go!”
“Ohh my my my.”
Right after that, a mysterious electric shock crackled through my body, and my consciousness faded away.
---
“Ugh... where am I...”
I opened my eyes, thinking Usaunny had come to save me again, but there was no sign of it, and instead I woke up in some unfamiliar cave-like place. Come to think of it, Usaunny had only ever rescued me on land when it noticed some commotion involving an adventurer—it had never come to the sea. Worse, I found myself locked in a small cage. Damn... I couldn't die here. Back in the village, three young slave girls and a certain increasingly suspicious Usaunny, along with the Filolials, were waiting for me. No matter what, I had to survive! And so began my escape plan—
=====
April Fools' Day
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

title: Reuniting Once Again

While I waited like that… a carriage driven by a familiar-looking demi-human came clip-clopping toward the fort. Squinting, I could see that Father appeared to be aboard. It didn’t seem like anything in particular had gone wrong, I say.
“Wait just a moment, if you would!”
I swiftly canceled my concealment and stepped out in front of the carriage, raising a hand.
“Oh…? You’re the Spear Hero.”
“Eh? Motoyasu-kun?”
The carriage rumbled to a halt, and Father climbed down from it.
“It’s been two days. What’s wrong, Motoyasu-kun? Don’t tell me you came to see me off since I’m leaving the country?”
“There are various circumstances at play, indeed. So I’d like you to hear me out for a bit.”
“Eh? Sure…”
Ah, Father—how nostalgic. This was the very first Father from when the loop began, in a sense much like Fleon-chan was to me. I might have already met him while I was in a daze from the shock over Filo-tan, but even so, he was still my Father, I say.
“Father. Up ahead lies a tightly secured checkpoint, and there are those who’ve arranged to kill you the moment you try to leave the country.”
“Eh? Really? Well… given what you and the people of Siltvelt have told me, I figured something like that was possible, but I’d heard things were supposed to go peacefully.”
That would indeed be the case according to the Queen’s instructions. But there were countless people who simply weren’t listening to her.
“So what do we do? Should we take a detour, or sneak out of the country somehow…?”
“No need to worry about that, indeed. I’ve already gone and handled it in a flash.”
That fort was already empty as a husk.
“However, there are various complicated circumstances involved, I say. To tell you the truth, I’ve looped back in time since then.”
“Eh? You looped? What do you mean?”
“It’s a long story, but back then, I was in a situation where the moment any of the Four Cardinal Heroes died, I’d loop right back to right after the summoning. It seems Father must have died somewhere down the line, causing the loop. But this time, I came back to the day before that loop occurred.”
“I see… so there’s a lot of complicated stuff tangled up in this. Then I guess that means you came back through this loop to stop me from being killed.”
“Indeed.”
“In that case… taking into account everything you’ve learned from all these loops, what do you think we should do, Motoyasu-kun?”
Hmm… honestly speaking, the fort was already on the verge of falling, and using the portal, we could reach Siltvelt in an instant. Having reunited with Father meant safety was more or less guaranteed, so there were plenty of options available. Should I just send Father off to Siltvelt as things stood?
Ugh… my memories were a bit hazy on this, but I felt like I should search for a different approach than before. Above all, it might be worth trying out what I’d learned from Father and the others during that previous loop when everyone headed to Faubrey together. Memories of what happened with Ark were also surfacing in my mind. I recalled there being something I mustn’t let Father realize, something I shouldn’t teach him. But there were things I could still discuss with him.
“Father, I know you’re planning to head to Siltvelt, but I’d like you to come with me for now, I say.”
“Sure. If it’s a request from you, Motoyasu-kun, I’m happy to go along with it.”
“Ehh…”
At that, the Siltvelt envoy’s face twisted with visible trouble.
“I apologize for the sudden change of plans, indeed. But if we head straight to Siltvelt as planned, that too would cause problems down the line.”
“What sort of problems, might I ask?”
I explained to the Siltvelt envoy what would happen in the future. Well, as for the matter involving Takt, that I could crush ahead of time.
“It’s an outlandish tale, but I can indeed see it being plausible.”
“If I put my mind to it, I could get us there in an instant, indeed. But could you hold off on heading to Siltvelt for just a little while?”
“An instant… I have heard legends of the Heroes possessing such powers. Understood.”
“Well then, Father, shall we use the portal to rejoin Kuro-chan once more?”
“Sure, got it. Let’s head back for now, then—though it’ll be quite the round trip.”
“Indeed.”
Even as I thought this, I needed to properly sort out what could only be accomplished during this particular loop, right now. I would invite Father to join the party, and bring the Siltvelt envoy along as well.
“Shall we leave the carriage here for the time being?”
“No, I’ll have one of my subordinates deliver it to a nearby town. There’s a chance we might need it again later.”
“Indeed. Well then, let’s be off. Portal Spear!”
Fwoosh! In an instant, we made our round trip back to the castle town of Melromarc.
“Ohh… so this really can get us to Siltvelt in an instant.”
“I wasn’t able to manage that back then, I say.”
Such was the power of information gained through looping.
“It’s like these past two days of travel just vanished in a flash, but… well, I suppose that can’t be helped.”
“What did you do these past two days, Father?”
“After introducing myself to the Siltvelt envoy and their companions, we traveled slowly by carriage. We stopped at an inn along the way, but things got a bit noisy, so we kept moving a few times while staying cautious.”
I see. So a bit of a mix-up had occurred, then.
“Ah, Moto-oh, welcome back!”
Kuro-chan greeted us as we returned to the inn.
“Peep, peep!”
The Filolial-sama chicks greeted us as well. Since we hadn’t leveled up yet, they hadn’t grown at all.
“Oh, it’s Nao. Welcome back!”
“Um…”
Father tilted his head slightly, looking at Kuro-chan. It seemed he couldn’t quite connect Kuro-chan’s angel form with her Filolial form.
“Kuro-chan, why don’t you turn into your Filolial-sama form?”
“Okay!”
With a poof, Kuro-chan transformed into her Filolial form. Her appearance wasn’t all that different from Black Thunder’s. If anything, one might say her eyes gave off a gentler impression than Black Thunder’s.
“Whoa, it really is Kuro-chan!?”
“Yep. Something about the Love Hunter recalling his Destiny, so, nao—he went off chasing his Aegis.”
“Ah… I see. You use some pretty distinctive words, Kuro-chan.”
“Is it cool?”
“Y-yeah, sure. Have you been talking like that for a while now, I wonder…”
Having received words of praise from Father, Kuro-chan smiled happily.
“Filolials really are amazing. You said you were searching for Filo-chan, Motoyasu-kun—how’s that going? Any luck finding her?”
“Of course, I’ve managed to find Filo-tan.”
“That’s good to hear.”
That’s right. Filo-tan was Sakura-chan. And in this loop, Sakura-chan hadn’t hatched yet. Which meant this was a loop where she could still become Filo-tan for me as well.
What fortunate timing, I say. “So Elmelo-chan’s a good fit too.”
“For now, yes. There’s a more dynamic way to push Elmelo-san further, but… right now she’s split between the ‘caged beast’ exhibit and performing tricks alongside the Filolials in the show.”

Elephant answered with a wry little laugh. Any customer rude enough to try that got a stern warning from me, I say. It seemed that former soldiers and officers who’d fought in the war against Siltvelt knew all too well how dangerous Elephant could be.

“No doubt she’d be excellent material for the act—nimble hands, great at leaping about. Not to mention she’s quite good with numbers, I say.”
“I get that she’d be perfect for scouting, but there’s no getting around the fact that we don’t have one…”
Tch! The sting of my failed scouting attempt still lingered. I’d been certain that if Father himself made the offer, it’d be a done deal.
“Now that I think of it, apparently there’s someone from Panda’s hometown living in the castle town. Shall we go have a word with them? We’ll need to track them down first, though.”
Where on earth would they even be running a shop, I wondered.
“You mean Lars has relatives here?”
Apparently Elephant hadn’t known that either.
“Hmm…”
“Or perhaps we could head straight to Panda’s home village instead?”
I did have a Portal on hand, so we could get there in a flash.
“Motoyasu-kun, you seem to know a suspicious amount about this person.”
“Father and I have crossed paths so many times it’s practically fate by this point, I say. I’ve got their whole family situation memorized from the loops.”
Come to think of it, I really did need to arrange an introduction between Trash and Tiger Girl—the daughter of Panda’s first love. But with the Crimson Swine currently residing in Melromarc’s castle, showing her off there was clearly out of the question. I recalled how even Siltvelt’s envoy had worn a sour expression, uneasy about a member of Tiger Girl’s race falling under Father’s banner. If the Crimson Swine ever learned of Tiger Girl’s existence, she wouldn’t hesitate for a second before plotting her murder. Even I wouldn’t stoop to something so vile. First, I’d see to the Crimson Swine’s removal—then present Tiger Girl to Trash and crush what fighting spirit he had left.
“Lars… there’s no escaping it, is there. Just how much do you know about me?”
“Ohh?”
“For that matter, I know everything about Elephant’s family too, I say.”
“Ugh… please, I beg you, don’t say anything.”
Oh dear, Elephant had stopped me cold. And here I’d been about to turn it into quite the heroic tale.
“Well, Elephant’s family matters can wait until Melromarc’s affairs are settled, I say.”
“Please, just stop…”

“Older Sister was busy looking for Big Sister, I say.”

“Nothing else, no.”
“Ohh, is that so. Well, Big Sister’s glad she never had such a rough past like Elmelo-chan’s.”
“You…”
Elephant stared at Older Sister with a look of pure exasperation. Come to think of it, I never really understood Older Sister all that well. All I knew was that she’d been close with Big Sister’s parents once.
“Now, now… Motoyasu-kun genuinely means well toward Elmelo-san, so I don’t think he’d ever actually do anything to trouble her, right?”
“I do hope that’s the case…”

“No problem at all, I say. Panda’s grandfather currently wields ki even more powerfully than Panda herself. Scouting the grandfather in her place is also an option, I say.”
Would you cut that out already! Panda seemed to protest inside my head, but that was surely just my imagination.
“Panda’s village is full of pandas, I say.”
“Whoa… sounds like a dream destination.”
Father seemed positively delighted at the thought of visiting a village full of pandas.
“Come to think of it, Panda’s grandfather has a long-standing rival in an old woman from Melromarc—whenever the two meet, they happily beat each other senseless, I say.”
“There’s a person like that too? New information just keeps piling up here.”
“Indeed… the old woman makes for an excellent combat advisor in every single loop, I say. She’s currently weakened by illness, but if Father performs a good deed and gets her to drink the medicine, she’ll cooperate wholeheartedly, from the bottom of her heart.”
“Wait, doesn’t that mean, in game terms, my Good Deed Points aren’t high enough to recruit her?”
Oh? Was that actually a possibility?
“Well, curing the illness fully does take a bit of time, but I believe persistence will see it through, I say.”
It seemed that directly curing her illness was itself enough to earn her deep gratitude.
“I’m not too confident about that one… if I go in relying on loop knowledge without care, the recruitment’s probably going to fail.”
“Indeed, given how badly the attempt with Lars went, it’s certainly plausible.”
Ngh… I say.
“That’s true. Even after Motoyasu-kun helped me, trusting him took quite a lot of doing.”
“So what shall we do, then?”
“Um… the panda village does sound kind of interesting. The old woman’s case seems like it needs good deeds first, but for the panda, maybe just talking with the daughter directly would work out.”
“Well, I think Lars will take the job as long as you pile on enough gold. It’s really just that she misunderstood the Spear Hero-sama’s negotiation tactics.”
“Motoyasu-kun, exactly what kind of negotiation did you do?”
“Nothing at all out of the ordinary, I say.”
“No… it came across more like elder care—including in a rather sexual sense, if I’m being honest.”
What, my recruitment pitch had been taken that way? Now that I thought about it, Panda had indeed given some rather suggestive-sounding responses at the time.
“Motoyasu-kun. Did you introduce me as some sort of elderly man? Or rather, what exactly did you say to this panda person about me…”
“It’s a misunderstanding, I say.”
“The real issue was how Spear Hero-sama referred to Shield Hero-sama.”
“Ah… I see, that would explain it if you don’t know the context. I thought so too… and she kept pressing me rather persistently about my virginity, so now I’m a little suspicious about whether it really was just a misunderstanding.”
Father had drifted off into some sort of melancholy for reasons unknown. Regardless, I couldn’t afford to let my reputation sink any further!
“Well then, shall we at least go and pay our respects?”
“Sure, even just as a traveler passing through by chance is fine—I’d like to see it. Panda’s village.”
“Understood. Then let us depart, I say.”

Naofumi Iwatani | Status: Peckul | Class: Shield Hero | Lv. 1 | Equipment: Small Shield (Legendary Weapons) | Skills: None | Magic: None

Don’t strike a pose right there, Rabbit Motoyasu—you’re definitely enjoying this situation, aren’t you?

Itsuki looked annoyed by Motoyasu the Rabbit’s provocation.

“I truly believe that. Well, though I doubt it’ll actually work.”

Usagi Motoyasu laughed heartily, “HAHAHA.” He’s nice to me, but he’s so provocative toward Itsuki… I wonder if it’s some kind of rodent pride?
“Since it looks like there’s a party feature, I’ll go ahead and form a party.”
With a *pop*, Motoyasu the Rabbit fiddled with something, and a party invitation appeared on my status icon, so I accepted it. It’s just like forming a party in an online game. Then, Motoyasu the Rabbit gave his spear a light swing… and when he gripped it, I had the illusion that our figures had become somewhat translucent. Was it just my imagination?

A man who looked like a king was striding purposefully, leading his soldiers and taking control of the castle gate. Could that guy actually be the king?

Shushu! Motoyasu the rabbit is showing some enthusiasm, but honestly, right after being summoned—at Level 1—it’s probably impossible for us. I mean, he might have enough initial Attack Power to impale us, but still.
“No… let’s hold off on that.”
“In classic games like this, castles usually have secret passages, right?”
If an event like this happened out of the blue, in a game, the story would usually lead to an escape route through a different choice.

“Then let’s head over there. I’m sure there’s an underground passage.”

So, we went underground, but… it turns out this was an underground prison, and there were prisoners locked up in cells. Maybe it’s a good thing, but none of them are looking our way.

Half of the prisoners had animal ears. Some even had features that made them look almost entirely like animals. Wow… Beastmen. I’m kind of the same right now, though. We’ve also shrunk a bit.
“We probably shouldn’t just go around trying to rescue them, right?”
“Yeah. We might get attacked out of the blue, and if we get caught up in a commotion, those guys will notice us.”
Holding our breath and searching for an escape route, we made our way through the underground prison… but before we knew it, Motoyasu the Rabbit had taken the lead. Soon… Motoyasu the Rabbit’s ears twitched as he spotted one of the cells. The semi-transparent aura around it vanished in an instant. Then Motoyasu the Rabbit peered into the cell.
“Hm? It’s been noisy for a while now… A Beastman? Were they brought here by the soldiers? It’s deplorable that the people of this country have even rounded up such small creatures.”
Inside the cell was… a beautiful woman—she looked like a female knight—hanging with her arms bound by chains. Itsuki looked back and forth between me and the woman who looked like a knight.
“She seems like someone we can talk to. Should we ask her some questions to get a handle on the situation?”

“I guess so… I don’t think it’d be a bad idea to talk to her. Here.”
“Please let me handle this, pyon!”
“I’m a little nervous about leaving it to Motoyasu. Naofumi-san, as the next-eldest here. Can I count on you?”
“Got it.”
So, I decided to step up as the spokesperson and ask the woman who looked like a knight.
“I’d prefer if you could just stay quiet for now, though. We were suddenly summoned from another world, nearly killed by the summoners, and barely managed to escape here.”
“What? What do you mean… Wait, you guys, those weapons you’re holding…”

Just as I said that, Motoyasu—the rabbit—started rolling his spear back and forth, changing its shape. Oh, I saw that in the help section. It said that if you insert materials, the weapon unlocks and you can change its form. When did he even insert the materials?
“Those characteristics match the hero from legend… Could it be that the commotion earlier was caused by a Beastman being summoned as the hero!?”

I see! So, in this country, humans are the embodiment of justice, and the Hero—who is an object of worship—appeared as a Beastman, a member of an enemy race.
“They’re probably trying to cover up the fact that a Beastman Hero was summoned…”
“That’s a plausible explanation.”
“They’ll be desperate to kill us.”
“But what should we do? Going in head-on is out of the question—the security is way too tight…”
“If I were to leave here and speak to the king… well, it’d be tough for a hero who’s a Beastman. This country is that harsh on Beastmen and Demi-Humans. I, too, am currently imprisoned for taking the law into my own hands against those who hunted down Demi-Humans as slaves in my father’s fiefdom—a place known for its friendship with Demi-Humans—which was devastated by the Wave.”
Wow… this person seems like a pretty decent person. If it’s true, I’d like to help him.
“The Wave…”
It’s the same disaster mentioned in the *Book of the Four Holy Weapons* I read.
“Ah, my father’s territory was devastated by the Wave. Presumably, a Hero will be summoned to save the world from this crisis. You two were summoned for that… but since our races are inconvenient for the country, we were almost killed on the spot.”
I see… So that’s why we’re being targeted and are barely managing to escape like this.
“It’s quite a twist of fate that the hero is a Beastman… I think it would be right to hand the hero over to another country, but the kingdom probably won’t allow it.”
“Um… my name is Naofumi. And you are?”
“…Eclair Seaetto.”
So, Ms. Eclair.
“I sense a draft over here. I’m sure there’s a secret escape route.”
“Well then…”
“No, wait… Could you take me with you? I’d like you to serve as my escort. I had intended to wait until the queen returned, but it seems I can’t afford to wait any longer.”
We all look at each other.
“What should we do? She seems to know the situation fairly well, and I don’t get the impression she’s guilty of anything serious.”
“From the looks of it, she seems to be human. If we get out of here, we won’t be able to get supplies in town, so if she’s willing to help us, it might be a good idea.” “The problem is the wanted poster and all that, but according to what we’ve heard, she’s a noblewoman—maybe she has some allies?”
“What should we do?”
Hmm… It’s one event after another, but I’m actually getting a little excited. It feels like it’s all been set up—as if someone who seems to be on our side and doing the right thing has been captured. She reminds me of the female knight from the sixth volume of *The Last Illusion*, so I feel like it might be okay to take her with us.
“There’s a chance she’ll betray us the moment we save her, though…”
“There’s no end to being suspicious. We’ve got no choice but to run anyway.”
“You’re right…”
“Well then, let’s go save her!”
With a sharp slash, Motoyasu cuts through the metal bars of the cell and frees Eclair.
“Thank you.”
“I think there’s an escape route ahead, so let’s go.”
“Yeah. I’ll bring up the rear.”
So, relying on Motoyasu’s keen hearing, we made our way through the underground tunnels and emerged into what looked like a waterway. There was a locked section along the way, but Motoyasu physically cut through it with his spear so we could pass.
“It seems they’ve noticed we escaped into the waterway.”
Motoyasu twitched his ears, having sensed it.
“Are we okay?”
“They’re still way behind us. We’ll make it out alive. Even if they catch up, we’ll just take them out. Don’t underestimate a hero, pyon.”
Thinking to myself, “Wow, we’re moving through this pretty easily,” we followed Motoyasu’s lead down the waterway.
“I think it’d be best if my Father carried us from here on, pyon.”
Then, at a spot where we could see a light and the current was getting a bit faster, Motoyasu made a suggestion.
“Ah, if Mr. Naofumi the penguin guides us, I think we can make it.”
“I don’t want to.”
For some reason, Ren refused right then and there.
“Why not? We’re almost out of here.”
“You guys get out there; I’m taking a different route.”
What on earth is going on? We were all set to go together just a moment ago—why the sudden change?
“You can’t swim, can you?! Hahahaha!”
Motoyasu clutched his stomach and laughed, pointing at Ren, who began to tremble uncontrollably.
“That’s not it! I can swim!”
“…It looks like he’s hit the nail on the head.”
“That’s why I’m saying I can swim! This is ridiculous.”
“But if we go back the way we came, we might run into the soldiers. I’ll carry you, so just stay still.”
“Whoa! Don’t pick me up! I can swim!”
“Lord Iwatani, can you take the lead?”
“Got it. Alright, everyone, let’s go.”
“Yeah.”
“Let’s go!”
And so, Itsuki and Motoyasu followed right behind me… but Itsuki’s cheeks puffed out like a swim ring.
“Whoa! What’s going on! My cheeks are puffing out on their own—”
“Ugh, seriously… I’ll carry you, so just stay still.”
“You’re making a pretty good life preserver.”
Eclair-san held Itsuki like a life preserver and carried Ren on her back. Ren… was perched on Eclair-san’s shoulder as if determined not to get wet. Just like that, we swam all the way through the waterway and made it out to the open air.
“I have no idea why my cheek pouches suddenly puffed up—this is a total mess.”
“How about that! I didn’t drown, did I?”
“Ren, I get that you don’t like water, so please be quiet. I’m the one in serious trouble here.”
“Never mind that—we’re out now. We need to make a quick getaway.”
After leaving the waterway, Eclair draped a ragged cloth she’d found along the way over herself, and we hid inside it as we made our way through the castle town, trying to avoid being noticed. It seemed soldiers were setting up a tight cordon around the castle. Furthermore… there were wanted posters up with sketches that looked just like us.
“These are the vicious Beastmen who infiltrated the castle. Report them the moment you spot them, and kill them no matter what! Don’t listen to a word these guys say! They’re vicious criminals who’ve killed dozens of people inside the castle.”
Motoyasu and Ren attacked them so fiercely they couldn’t move, but I doubt they actually killed them… I didn’t know what happened to the knight who let out that bloodcurdling scream, but it was still within the range where he could be treated. This is another world, so there must be healing magic, right?
“Eclair-san.”
“What is it?”
“Is there such a thing as healing magic?”
“Yes, there is.”
That’s a relief. Then that knight probably isn’t dead either.
“In any case, we’d better hurry out of the castle town—before the gates close.”
“You’re right, Eclair.”
“Got it. Everyone, hold on to me. Let’s hurry.”
“Let’s go!”
Then, as Motoyasu gripped his spear again, I felt as if we’d become semi-transparent. Just like that, we managed to make it out of the castle town.
“Now that we’re this far, I guess we can breathe a sigh of relief… maybe.”
“I hope so… but what should we do now?”
“Let’s go to someone I know. There’s a person there who shares the same ideals as my father, who has a deep understanding of Demi-Humans and Beastmen. If we can get their cooperation, that should work out. Right now, the castle guards are too busy investigating the castle town, so if we move while they’re occupied, we shouldn’t have any trouble.”
“You’re right. Then, please lead the way.”
And so, guided by Ms. Eclair, we set off.
The sun was setting… and since we were completely penniless, we decided to avoid attention and spend the night outdoors… We chatted with everyone around the campfire. Dinner? Since everyone had helped defeat the monsters we’d encountered, I cooked the meal, and we all ate together. I’d managed to get my hands on a knife while we were fleeing, so I was glad I could use it. Though, when I thought I could fight with this knife and tried to grip it, it bounced right off my hand—turns out I can only use it as a shield.
“Phew… These skewers tasted better than I expected.”
“It was great that we could use the medicinal herbs we found along the way as seasoning.”
“Naofumi, you’re a great cook.”
“It’s not that great.”
Sitting in front of the crackling campfire, I feel a bit excited—even if it’s a bit inappropriate. My heart was in my throat at first… but when I think about being in another world on an adventure, it feels like a dream.
“I’m going to the bathroom for a bit.”
“Ah, Motoyasu-san, are you going for another meal? Make sure to freshen up your breath, okay?”
Itsuki made a remark to Motoyasu that bordered on provocation.
“HAHAHA, I’m not eating, you know? Well then, I’ll be off.”
With that, Motoyasu rustled off. He didn’t come back for quite a while.
“Motoyasu, I wonder what on earth he’s doing?”
---
“I’m back. I took the opportunity to scout the area.”
“Oh… is that so? Any signs of soldiers?”
“None at all.”
That’s the most important thing. By the way, as for what he was actually doing later on… well, it seems this guy—the root of all our troubles—had gone to rescue the girl. He’ll be introduced later. In any case, exhausted as we were, we took turns resting as our life on the run continued. We hitched a ride on a shared horse-drawn carriage in a village along the way. It was my first time riding in a covered wagon. It looks like our life on the run will continue for a while yet… but somehow we ended up agreeing that we should head for either the country of Faubrey or the country of Siltvelt. According to Ms. Eclair, heading to Faubrey would be best, but since escaping from Melromarc is the priority for now… our journey continues. And so, together with my reliable companions, the curtain rose on an adventure that, while terrible, also looked like it would be fun.

And so, for that reason, I brought Father and the others along to Panda’s village. How nostalgic, I say. One way or another, ever since Panda and Father grew close, this village has become a place we visit more and more often. Depending on the circumstances, it’s even become something of a leisurely getaway spot, indeed. In the previous loop, Father used to come here to relax and unwind too. It seemed like he alternated between mooching off Big Sister’s village and this one.
“Ohh… so many pandas. It’s like some kind of dream place.”
I could see Father’s eyes positively sparkling. He always looks so delighted like this.
“There’s even a bamboo grove! It really feels like the sort of place you’d imagine! Waah… what a dream come true.”
As Father walked toward the village looking all around, a village panda near the entrance noticed us.
“Oh my? Travelers, perhaps?”
The village panda addressed us with a somewhat wary air.
“Ah, yes. We’re travelers—we heard there was a village here and decided to stop by.”
Father handled the village panda with his business smile. The village panda looked Father up and down, then turned its gaze to me, Elephant, and Older Sister. After that, it stared intently at Father. Probably wondering why on earth a human would come here. Apparently, demi-humans and beastmen also tend to feel some strange sensation upon first meeting Father, aside from that suspicion. According to Father, it’s likely something to do with the power of the Shield’s sacred weapon or some such.
“I see… welcome, then. It must have been quite a journey to get here. Travelers, we can’t offer much of a warm welcome, but please, rest easy in the village.”
“Yes, thank you very much.”
With that exchange of greetings, the village panda hurried off toward the grandfather panda’s house. Presumably to report that some unfamiliar folks had shown up.
“So this is Lars’s hometown… honestly, there’s no other way to put it—there really are a ton of Lars’s kin here.”
Elephant nodded, looking around, seeming convinced.
“Ohh, I wonder if this village has any local specialty sake?”
Older Sister seemed preoccupied with sake, as always. I recalled her searching for sake here before too. I think there was indeed some brewed locally. If we asked, surely they’d sell us some? Then again, now that I thought about it, I’d never actually come to this village without Panda along. No telling how things would go, but no matter—there shouldn’t be any real problems, I say.
“Man, for a panda lover, this place is basically paradise, huh.”
“And what about you, Naofumi-chan?”
“I mean, sure, pandas are cute, right? Though apparently zoo pandas have pretty sharp-looking eyes most of the time—but whenever I went, I never saw that kind of expression on them.”
Father regaled us with a story about seeing pandas at the zoo. Apparently, after eating bamboo, one had looked like it was waving at him, which he’d found delightful. Also, apparently a panda had come up to sniff at him through the glass, and everyone had swarmed for the photo opportunity, shoving him right out of line.
“So yeah, at the zoo I never really got to see them up close like that.”
A cheerful little anecdote from Father. As for me, whenever I went on dates with pigs, I always seemed to end up watching the pig far more than the actual animals. I knew perfectly well that if I kept staring at the animals too long, the pig would get sulky. Honestly, at that rate there’s hardly any difference between an amusement park and a zoo—it’s basically a pig farm, I say. It seemed like Father was having a much more enjoyable time than I ever had, which stirred up a bit of envy in me. And so, chatting like this, we wandered the panda village in search of an establishment—an inn, a tavern, that sort of thing. Even small villages tend to have a tavern or two, serving as a communal gathering spot for the villagers. I’d been to this village a few times before, so I had a decent grasp of the terrain, but for Father and the others, this was their first time. Still, since we usually stayed at Panda’s house as our base, now that we’d come as ordinary travelers, checking out the tavern seemed the thing to do. We stepped into a cozy little tavern. It likely doubled as an inn too—ask nicely, and they’d probably let us stay the night.
“Looks like Elmelo-san won’t be able to fit in… though it is bigger than the taverns in Melromarc.”
Elephant, being an oversized beastman, needed a correspondingly large tavern to fit into.
“Don’t worry about it. I’m used to sleeping outdoors.”
“Even so, you know…”
“Ohh~”
And so, while our lodging plans remained undecided, we stood outside the tavern chatting when Panda’s foster father approached. A peacock beastman. Well, having some familiarity with him from the previous loop as well, I recognized him readily as Panda’s foster father.
“Good afternoon. It’s quite rare indeed for travelers to visit this village.”
“Ah, good afternoon. Yes, we heard there was a village here and decided to stop by.”
Father responded to Panda’s foster father’s greeting with a smile.
“So then, travelers, what business brings you here? If you’re in some kind of trouble, I’d be happy to lend an ear.”
Apparently, Panda’s foster father served as the village’s customer service and diplomatic liaison of sorts. He’d ask travelers their business, judge whether they posed a threat, and if it turned out to be commercial in nature, handle the negotiations accordingly. Father seemed to have sensed as much too, glancing at the rest of us before responding on our behalf with his business smile toward Panda’s foster father.
“Well, half of it is simple curiosity, and the other half—we heard there was a formidable warrior living in this village, and we thought we might get the chance to speak with them a little. Ah, please don’t be alarmed. We have absolutely no intention of picking a fight.”
Later, Father would tell me he’d judged it better to be upfront rather than spin some clumsy excuse.
“Hmm… I have no idea of any warrior in this village so formidable that travelers would hear tell of them. I’d like to know a bit more—where exactly did you hear such a rumor, and just who might this person be?”
“Well, it was just a rumor, really—if you’re asking who told us, it was merely something we overheard in the nearest town. It’s all quite uncertain, honestly.”
Ohh… there was Father’s business-customer-service mode in full swing. He deflected Panda’s foster father’s attempt to pin down the source of the rumor with a vague answer. I would have been perfectly willing to testify myself, but Father signaled me with his hand beforehand to hold my tongue, so I kept quiet.
“Going out of your way to verify a mere rumor—my, how diligent of you.”
Panda’s foster father responded with crackling wariness. It seemed he’d seen through the true intent behind Father’s evasiveness.
“Ohh~”
“Hmm…”
Older Sister and Elephant seemed to have sensed the tension too, and chose to hold their tongues, watching how things would unfold.
“As for the content of the rumor—apparently, long ago, this person was quite the formidable fighter, but has since retired and now lives here in this village.”
“That would make them quite elderly indeed. They may well have already passed away.”
An indirect way of saying he had no intention of introducing anyone. Was this a move to keep Father from meeting Panda’s grandfather?
“Is that so? Well, if that’s the case, wouldn’t there at least be some tale told of them in the village? I’d be glad to offer a prayer at their grave, if nothing else.”
Here, Father pressed further still. Panda’s foster father’s eyes seemed to narrow just slightly. I’d always thought of him as a gentle, child-loving sort, but apparently he had this side to him as well.
“Waah, travelers~?”
Just then, a little baby panda peeked out to look at us. Noticing the voice, Father smiled and gave a small wave. Panda’s foster father, as if signaling caution, ruffled his tail feathers and seemed to be trying to usher the child away. Father, sensing this too, nodded in understanding—no need to be wary, we mean no harm. Hmm… without Panda along, the wariness here felt awfully strong, and it didn’t seem like the conversation was going anywhere. Or… was it actually progressing, somehow?

“I think it’s going well, I say.”
I felt like I was managing to act differently than before. And within that, I intended to keep taking different actions going forward.
“Vau, vau.”
Just then, Wolf found Father, came into the tent, and started nuzzling up to him.
“There, there, Wolf. You fought well today, waited patiently, enjoyed the party—you did a great job.”
“Wa-owwn! Vau vau!”
Wolf struck a flexing pose while looking in the direction of the crocodile man.

“Vau.”
“Maybe sometime soon we could visit Éclair-san and Shion’s place.”
I think Father worries far too much about Éclair and the others, honestly.

All I remembered was Mole’s burrow itself. And more importantly, none of the moles had ever said anything about it.

It was starting to look like some strange factions were forming. To think Ren would cooperate with Assistant and the dragon. Luna-chan was glaring resentfully at the parent controlling Rival’s body. “A trap!?”

“Everyone, look at your feet! There are tons of things tied together with grass! And if you look closely, there are even thin cords laid out!”

Well, if they came strutting up spouting nonsense about holy war, I figured we could just wipe them all out and eliminate the troublemakers in one go. That moment was probably just a little ways off. It had become plain as day that Trash’s position was falling apart. And so… the time for the wave drew near.

The heroes gathered for a strategy meeting inside the circus over in Zeltoble.
“I’ll sink it in a flash, I say.”
Since there was no doubt this was a wave Rival might show up to, I had to sink it quickly before she could get here.
“That’s probably the safest bet.”

“Ah, I recall hearing something about that.”
“Hand over some of the materials.”
“I’ll spare you some, I say.”

Back then… I’d sunk the wave in a flash, and at the same time Itsuki had attacked, only for me to strike him down and take him captive. That he was now here participating in our strategy meeting—that really said something about how much circumstances could change.
